definition_zh: 交叉路口；汇合处；连接；连接点
definition_en: a place where roads, railway lines or wires meet or are joined together
core_image: 两条铁轨在信号灯前合到同一条线上，随后又各自分开
scene: 列车在路口前放慢速度。The train slowed down as it approached a busy junction outside the city.
sceneCN: 这里 junction 是「交叉路口」（第 1 个义项：道路或铁路交会的地点）；句意：列车在接近城郊一处繁忙的交叉路口时减慢了速度。

pos.zh: 交叉路口；汇合处；连接；连接点

derivatives.zh: 前缀 con-（一起）加同根名词构成，义为「连词；结合；合取」
前缀 dis-（分开）加同根名词构成，义为「分离；析取」
同词根名词，加 -ture 后缀，义为「接合点；紧要关头」
前缀 ad-（附加于）加同根词干构成，义为「附属物；附加语」

senses.title: A point where roads or tracks meet
senses.definition: a place where two or more roads or railway lines meet and split
senses.definitionCN: 两条或更多道路、铁路线相交并再次分开的地点
senses.example: Slow down before the junction and check both ways.
senses.exampleCN: 到路口前要减速，两边都要看清楚。
senses.why: Latin iunctio names a joining, so the place where lines join is the most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iunctio 本义就是「接合」，因此几条线相接的地点就是最字面的义项。

senses.title: A connection between parts
senses.definition: the point or manner in which two parts are linked together
senses.definitionCN: 两个部件相连的位置或方式
senses.example: Check the junction between the pipe and the tap.
senses.exampleCN: 检查一下水管和水龙头接合的地方。
senses.why: Beyond real roads, the word names any place where two parts are linked.
senses.whyCN: 离开真实道路之后，这个词就用来指任何两个部件相连的位置，因此有「接合处」。

senses.title: A box linking electrical conductors
senses.definition: a small box or device where electric wires are joined
senses.definitionCN: 把电线连接到一起的小盒子或装置
senses.example: A loose junction in the ceiling caused the light to flicker.
senses.exampleCN: 天花板上一处松动的接线处让灯闪烁不停。
senses.why: The physical joining sense moves into wiring, where a junction is exactly the box that ties wires together.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的「接合」延伸到电路里，接线盒正是把电线系在一起的那个接合点，于是有了这个义项。

senses.title: A point of contact or interplay between things
senses.definition: a point where two subjects, fields or processes meet and influence each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个学科、领域或过程相遇并相互影响的交汇点
senses.example: The seminar explored the junction between medicine and law.
senses.exampleCN: 这场研讨会探讨了医学与法律之间的交汇处。
senses.why: Once the word names where two roads meet, it can also name where two fields meet.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指两条路相交的地方，它也就顺理成章地指两个领域相遇之处。

intro.en: Junction comes from Latin iunctio, a joining, from iungere, to join or yoke, the same root that gives join and joint.
intro.cn: junction 来自拉丁语 iunctio（接合），源于 iungere（连接、套轭），与 join、joint 同根。

items.en: The reconstructed form yewg- meant to join or yoke animals together.
items.cn: 重构形式 yewg- 意为把动物套在一起、连接。

items.en: Iungere means to join, and iunctio means a joining.
items.cn: 拉丁语 iungere 意为连接，iunctio 意为接合。

items.en: The joining word reached French as jonction.
items.cn: 表示接合的词作为 jonction 进入法语。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the early seventeenth century in the general sense of joining.
items.cn: 这个词在十七世纪初进入英语，最初泛指「连接」。

items.en: Steam railways make the junction a standard word for a point where lines branch.
items.cn: 蒸汽铁路使 junction 成为铁路分岔点的常用词。

note.en: Junction lives in the join family, while its near meanings name places where lines or paths meet.
note.cn: junction 属于「连接」词族，它的近义词则是别的表示线路或路径相交的说法。

entries.definitionCN: 事物相接之处，或紧要关头

entries.definition: a joining together, or a word that joins clauses
entries.definitionCN: 结合；连词

entries.definition: something added to another thing but not essential
entries.definitionCN: 附加的东西；附属物

entries.definition: a point where two lines or roads cross
entries.definitionCN: 两条线或道路交叉的点

entries.definition: a place where two roads cross
entries.definitionCN: 两条道路交叉的十字路口

entries.definition: a place where two parts are fitted together
entries.definitionCN: 两个部分接合的地方；关节

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the join root, the railway picture and the everyday phrases road junction and at the junction of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子围绕「连接」词根、铁路画面以及 road junction、at the junction of 两个常用说法展开。

normal.en: The root iungere means to join or yoke, so a junction is simply where things are joined.
normal.cn: 词根 iungere 意为连接、套轭，junction 就是东西被接上之处。

normal.en: Join, joint, juncture and conjunction all come from the same Latin verb.
normal.cn: join、joint、juncture 与 conjunction 都出自同一个拉丁动词。

normal.en: A road junction is the standard phrase for a place where streets meet.
normal.cn: road junction 是「街道相交处」的标准说法。

normal.en: At the junction of two streets names the meeting point of named roads.
normal.cn: at the junction of 用来指出两条具名街道相交的位置。

normal.en: A railway junction is the standard term for a station where a line branches.
normal.cn: railway junction 是「铁路支线分岔站」的标准说法。

abstract.en: Two steel tracks slide together in front of a signal, then split again.
abstract.cn: 信号灯前，两条铁轨先并到一起，随后又各自分开。

abstract.en: A cable box on a wall ties several coloured wires into one knot.
abstract.cn: 墙上一个接线盒把几根彩色电线系成一处。

abstract.en: Two maps laid over each other overlap along one bright street.
abstract.cn: 两张地图叠在一起，在一条明亮的街道上重合。

examples.en: The main road bends sharply at the junction with the coast road.
examples.cn: 主干道在与滨海公路相交的路口急转弯。

examples.en: Cracks appeared at the junction of the two walls.
examples.cn: 两堵墙交接的地方出现了裂缝。

examples.en: Engineers repaired the junction where the old tunnel meets the new line.
examples.cn: 工程师们修好了旧隧道与新线路相接的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「准克绳」——两条绳子在这里被「准」确地「克」住系紧；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 iungere（连接、套轭）→ iunctio（接合）→ 古法语 jonction → 英语 junction；同根词有 join、joint、juncture、conjunction、adjunct。

sensesIntro.en: Junction begins with a point where roads or rails join, spreads to any mechanical join, to electric wiring, and finally to a meeting point of ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: junction 先从道路或铁路相接的点说起，再扩展到任何部件的接合、电线的接点，最后落到思想与领域的交汇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rails sliding together before a signal and splitting again.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条铁轨在信号灯前先并到一起，随后又分开。

branches.en: Roads and rails meet at a named place.
branches.cn: 道路与轨道在具体地点相接。

branches.en: Any two parts can be joined.
branches.cn: 任何两个部件都能相接。

branches.en: Wires are tied in a small box.
branches.cn: 电线被系进一个小盒子里。

branches.en: Both mark a place where two ways come together.
branches.cn: 两者都标记两条路径相遇的地方。

branches.en: Both are physical joins between assembled pieces.
branches.cn: 两者都是装配件之间的物理接合。

intro.en: Junction is the noun of Latin iungere, to join, and it shares that root with join, joint, juncture, conjunction and adjunct.
intro.cn: junction 是拉丁语 iungere（连接）的名词形式，与 join、joint、juncture、conjunction、adjunct 共用这个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin iungere means to join, iunctio means a joining, and iunctura means a joint.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iungere 意为连接，iunctio 意为接合，iunctura 意为关节、接合处。

items.example: Iungere is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: iungere 是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Iunctio gives the modern noun.
items.exampleCN: iunctio 演变出现代的这个名词。

items.example: The suffix -tion forms junction and action.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成 junction 与 action。

items.example: Junct- appears in juncture and conjunction.
items.exampleCN: junct- 出现在 juncture 与 conjunction 里。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: The suffix -ture forms juncture.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ture 构成 juncture。

items.example: Con- plus junct- forms conjunction.
items.exampleCN: con- 加 junct- 构成 conjunction。

items.example: Dis- plus junct- forms disjunction.
items.exampleCN: dis- 加 junct- 构成 disjunction。

items.example: Ad- plus junct- forms adjunct.
items.exampleCN: ad- 加 junct- 构成 adjunct。

items.example: Junction is the everyday noun for a meeting point.
items.exampleCN: junction 是表示交汇点的日常名词。

definition_zh: 接合点；连接处；时刻，关头；接合
definition_en: a particular point in time, or a place where two things are joined together
core_image: 钟面上一条细线正好对上十二点，秒针在结点的瞬间停了一格
scene: 公司刚换了新老板。At this critical juncture, the whole team needs to stay calm.
sceneCN: 这里 juncture 是「关头、时刻」（第 2 个义项：某个特定的时间点）；句意：在这个紧要关头，整个团队都需要保持冷静。

pos.zh: 接合点；连接处；时刻；关头

derivatives.zh: 同词根名词，去掉 -ture 后缀，义为「路口；连接处」
基础词加 -al 形容词后缀构成，义为「接合的；关头的」（少见）
前缀 con-（一起）加同根词构成，义为「局面；时势」

senses.title: A joint or place where parts meet
senses.definition: a place or line where two parts are joined together
senses.definitionCN: 两个部分相接的地方或接缝
senses.example: Rain had seeped into the juncture of the roof and the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水渗进了屋顶与墙体相接的地方。
senses.why: Latin iunctura literally means a joint, so the most direct sense is the place where two parts meet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iunctura 本义就是「接合处、关节」，所以最直接的义项就是两个部分相接的地方。

senses.title: A particular point in time
senses.definition: a particular moment or stage in a series of events
senses.definitionCN: 一连串事件中的某个特定时刻或阶段
senses.example: At this juncture she had to choose between duty and freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个当口，她必须在责任与自由之间做选择。
senses.why: A joint is where two pieces meet, and by metaphor the present moment is where the past meets the future.
senses.whyCN: 接合处是两块东西相遇的地方；把时间想成一条线，此刻正是过去与未来相接的那个结点，于是有了「时刻、关头」。

senses.title: The act or manner of joining
senses.definition: the way in which parts are put together or united
senses.definitionCN: 各部件被拼合、连接的方式
senses.example: The motorboat is strong only at the juncture of each panel.
senses.exampleCN: 这小艇的牢固程度全看各块板之间的接合。
senses.why: The -ture ending names a result or manner of an action, so juncture can also mean the joining itself.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ture 表示动作的结果或方式，因此 juncture 也能指「接合」这个行为本身。

senses.title: A point in speech where sound units meet
senses.definition: a point in speech where two sounds or words meet and may need careful sounding
senses.definitionCN: 语音中两个音或两个词相接的地方，常需特别发音
senses.example: The teacher showed the juncture where the two vowels run together.
senses.exampleCN: 老师指出了两个元音连读的那个音渡处。
senses.why: In phonetics the metaphor of a joint becomes precise, naming the seam between sounds and words.
senses.whyCN: 在语音学里，「接合处」的比喻被精确化，专指音与音、词与词之间的接缝。

intro.en: Juncture comes from Latin iunctura, a joint, from iungere, to join, and it shares that root with junction, join and joint.
intro.cn: juncture 来自拉丁语 iunctura（关节、接合），源于 iungere（连接），与 junction、join、joint 同根。

items.en: The reconstructed form yewg- meant to join or yoke animals together.
items.cn: 重构形式 yewg- 意为把动物套在一起、连接。

items.en: Iungere means to join and iunctura means a joint or a joining.
items.cn: 拉丁语 iungere 意为连接，iunctura 意为关节、接合。

items.en: The word appears in English for a joint, a hinge or a place where things are set together.
items.cn: 这个词在英语里出现，指关节、铰链或东西拼合的地方。

items.en: The metaphor of a joint gives the sense of a particular moment in a course of events.
items.cn: 「接合处」的比喻引申出「事件进程中的某个时刻」这一义项。

items.en: Linguists borrow the word for the point where sounds and words meet.
items.cn: 语言学家借用这个词，指声音与词相接的位置。

note.en: Juncture is the joint of the join family, while its near meanings describe other critical moments.
note.cn: juncture 是「连接」词族里的「关节」，它的近义词则描述别的关键时刻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the joint root, the phrase at this juncture and the near twin junction in view.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子围绕「关节」词根、at this juncture 这个说法，以及形近词 junction 展开。

normal.en: The Latin iunctura means a joint, so juncture and joint are cousins.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 iunctura 意为关节，所以 juncture 与 joint 是同族兄弟。

normal.en: The -ture ending points to a result, as in picture and signature.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ture 指向一个结果，就像 picture 与 signature 那样。

normal.en: At this juncture is the fixed phrase for at this point in time.
normal.cn: at this juncture 是固定说法，相当于「眼下、在这个关头」。

normal.en: A critical juncture is the phrasing used in reports and histories.
normal.cn: a critical juncture 是报告和历史叙述里常用的说法。

normal.en: Compare junction: junction is the point on a road, juncture is the joint or the moment.
normal.cn: 对比 junction：junction 多指路上的交汇点，juncture 多指接缝或时刻。

abstract.en: Picture a hinge where two boards are screwed together.
abstract.cn: 想象两块木板用合页拧在一起的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a clock hand resting on a marked hour.
abstract.cn: 想象时钟的指针正停在整点刻度上。

abstract.en: Picture a tailor joining two panels of cloth along one sewn seam.
abstract.cn: 想象裁缝沿着一条缝把两块布接起来。

examples.en: The two halves of the shell meet at a narrow juncture.
examples.cn: 贝壳的两半在一条窄窄的接缝处合拢。

examples.en: At that juncture the committee had not yet made a decision.
examples.cn: 在那个当口，委员会还没有做出决定。

examples.en: The report warns that the country faces a critical juncture in its history.
examples.cn: 报告警告说，这个国家正处在历史的紧要关头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「准克扯」——两样东西在这里被「准」确地「克」住、扯不开；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 iungere（连接、套轭）→ iunctura（关节、接合处）→ 英语 juncture，核心义「关节」；同根词有 junction、join、joint、conjunction。

sensesIntro.en: Juncture starts from the literal joint, widens to a point in time, then to the act of joining, and finally to a seam between sounds.
sensesIntro.cn: juncture 从字面的「接合处」出发，扩展到时间上的「时刻」，再回到「接合」的动作，最后落到语音里的音渡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock hand resting exactly on a marked hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针正好停在钟面的整点刻度上。

branches.en: A literal joint between parts.
branches.cn: 部件之间真实的接缝。

branches.en: The joint becomes a moment in time.
branches.cn: 接合处被想成时间上的一个点。

branches.en: The joining itself is named.
branches.cn: 「接合」这一行为被命名。

branches.en: Both concern how two parts are fastened.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及两个部分如何被固定到一起。

branches.en: Both are seams where separate units touch.
branches.cn: 两者都是彼此分离的单位相互接触的接缝。

intro.en: Juncture keeps the Latin joint root iunct-, here with the -ture ending that names a result, as in picture and signature.
intro.cn: juncture 保留拉丁语「接合」词根 junct-，并加上表示结果的词尾 -ture，就像 picture 与 signature。

latinIntro.en: Latin iungere means to join, iunctura a joint, and iunctio a joining.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iungere 意为连接，iunctura 意为关节，iunctio 意为接合。

items.exampleCN: iungere 是整个词族的词根。

items.exampleCN: iunctura 是 juncture 的直接蓝本。

items.meaning: result or means of an action

items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ture 构成 juncture 与 signature。

items.example: Junct- appears in junction and adjunct.
items.exampleCN: junct- 出现在 junction 与 adjunct 里。

items.example: Con- plus junct- forms conjunction.
items.exampleCN: con- 加 junct- 构成 conjunction。

items.example: The ending -ure also appears in measure.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ure 也出现在 measure 里。

items.example: The suffix -al forms junctural.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 junctural。

items.meaning: relating to a joint or a juncture
items.example: Junctural is a rare adjective from this noun.
items.exampleCN: junctural 是由这个词派生的生僻形容词。

items.example: Juncture keeps both the joint and the moment.
items.exampleCN: juncture 同时保留「关节」与「时刻」两义。

definition_zh: 法学；法理学；法律体系；判例理论
definition_en: the science or study of law, and also the legal theory behind how courts reason
core_image: 一位法官面前摊开法典，旁边堆着写满判词的卷宗
scene: 法学生在图书馆里翻着厚重的法学专著，想弄懂法院为何这样判决。The student turned to jurisprudence to understand why the court reasoned as it did.
sceneCN: 这里 jurisprudence 是「法学、法理学」（第 1 个义项：研究法律的学问）；句意：这名学生求助于法理学，想弄明白法院为何这样推理。

pos.zh: 法学；法理学；法律体系；判例理论

derivatives.zh: 精于法学的；懂事理的
法理学的
法学家；法律学者

senses.title: The study of law as a science
senses.definition: the systematic study of the nature, sources, and principles of law
senses.definitionCN: 对法律的性质、渊源与原则进行的系统研究
senses.example: He teaches jurisprudence at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 他在大学里教授法理学。
senses.why: The Latin roots join ius, meaning law, to prudentia, meaning knowledge, so the word first names the learned discipline that understands law.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根把 ius（法律）与 prudentia（知识、明智）接在一起，所以这个词最初指「懂法律的学问」，也就是研究法律本身的学科。

senses.title: A body of law in a country
senses.definition: the whole system of laws and legal decisions in a particular country or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 某一国家或法律传统中全部法律与判决构成的整体体系
senses.example: American and English jurisprudence differ on this point.
senses.exampleCN: 美国与英格兰的法律体系在这一点上有所不同。
senses.why: A discipline that classifies law naturally comes to name the classified body of law itself, especially in comparative legal writing.
senses.whyCN: 专门分类整理法律的学问，很自然会把整部被整理好的法律体系也表示出来，在比较法写作里尤其常见。

senses.title: The theory of legal reasoning
senses.definition: a particular school of legal thought, such as positivism, realism, or natural law theory
senses.definitionCN: 某一种法律思想流派，如法律实证主义、法律现实主义或自然法理论
senses.example: Legal realism reshaped American jurisprudence in the twentieth century.
senses.exampleCN: 法律现实主义在二十世纪重塑了美国的法律理论。
senses.why: Once the word names the study of legal principles, it can also mark one set of principles against another, giving us rival schools of jurisprudence.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指研究法律原理的学问，它也可以代表某套原理与其他原理相对，于是有了互相对立的法理学流派。

senses.title: Case law built from decisions
senses.titleCN: 判例法；法院判决形成的法律
senses.definition: the body of rulings that courts develop over time and later courts follow or distinguish
senses.definitionCN: 法院经年累月形成的判决体系，后来的法院会遵循或区分这些判例
senses.example: For years the courts added to a consumer protection jurisprudence.
senses.exampleCN: 多年来，法院不断丰富着保护消费者的判例集。
senses.why: Law understood as prudence in action shows up as the accumulated wisdom of judges, so the word can name the case law that reasoning produces.
senses.whyCN: 把法律理解为实践中的明智，就体现为法官日积月累的判断经验，所以这个词也可以指这些推理所产出的判例法。

senses.title: Legal philosophy in formal works
senses.definition: the branch of philosophy concerned with what law is and how it should be interpreted
senses.definitionCN: 哲学的一个分支，研究法律是什么、该如何被解释
senses.example: Her book belongs to the philosophy of jurisprudence rather than to practice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书属于法学理论，而不是实务。
senses.why: Inside the academy the discipline meets philosophy, and the word becomes a label for abstract questions about law rather than about particular statutes.
senses.whyCN: 在学院内部，这门学问与哲学接壤，于是这个词成了追问法律抽象问题的标签，而不是讨论某部具体法规。

intro.en: Jurisprudence pairs the Latin ius, meaning law, with prudentia, meaning knowledge or foresight, and English borrowed it from French legal usage.
intro.cn: jurisprudence 把拉丁语 ius（法律）和 prudentia（知识、明智）接在一起，英语借自法语的法律用法。

items.en: Ius names law or right, and prudentia names knowledge or practical wisdom.
items.cn: ius 表示法律或权利，prudentia 表示知识或实践中的明智。

items.en: Iurisprudentia is the knowledge of the law held by Roman jurists.
items.cn: iurisprudentia 指罗马法学家所掌握的关于法律的知识。

items.en: Juriprudence carries the term into medieval French legal writing.
items.cn: juriprudence 把这个术语带入中世纪的法语法律文献。

items.en: The word is used for the study of law and later for the body of case law.
items.cn: 英语在十七至十八世纪用它指法律研究，后来又指判例体系。

items.en: American law schools make jurisprudence a subject about legal theory and reasoning.
items.cn: 美国法学院把 jurisprudence 设为一门讨论法律理论与推理的课程。

note.en: Jurisprudence shares the ius root with jurist and juridical, and stands beside law, legislation, and case law.
note.cn: jurisprudence 与 jurist、juridical 共享 ius 词根，并与 law、legislation、case law 相邻。

entries.definition: an expert in law
entries.definitionCN: 法学家；法律专家

entries.definition: relating to law or the administration of justice
entries.definitionCN: 法律的；司法的

entries.definition: careful good judgement
entries.definitionCN: 审慎；精明（与词尾 prudentia 同源）

entries.definition: the system of rules enforced by a state
entries.definitionCN: 国家强制执行的一整套规则

entries.definition: laws made by a parliament or similar body
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关制定的法律

entries.definition: a settled principle in law or thought
entries.definitionCN: 法律或思想中确立的原则；学说

normalIntro.en: Jurisprudence is law plus wisdom: the learned wisdom about law, ius joined to prudentia.
normalIntro.cn: jurisprudence 是「法律 + 智慧」：关于法律的学问与智慧，即 ius 加上 prudentia。

normal.en: The root ius means law, so every jur- word is about law.
normal.cn: 词根 ius 意为法律，所以每个 jur- 开头的词都与法律有关。

normal.en: Prudentia means prudence, so jurisprudence is the prudence of law.
normal.cn: prudentia 意为审慎，所以 jurisprudence 就是「法律的审慎」。

normal.en: Jurist names the expert in law; jurisprudence names the free-standing expert subject.
normal.cn: jurist 指法律专家；jurisprudence 指独立存在的专家学科。

normal.en: Medical jurisprudence was an older name for forensic medicine.
normal.cn: medical jurisprudence 是法医学的旧称。

normal.en: Compare law: law is the rules, jurisprudence is the study or theory of rules.
normal.cn: 对比 law：law 是规则本身，jurisprudence 是对规则的研究或理论。

abstract.en: Picture an old dictionary of law lying open beside a gavel.
abstract.cn: 想象一本翻开的旧法律词典摆在法槌旁边。

abstract.en: Imagine a map that draws the borders of every national legal system.
abstract.cn: 想象一张把所有国家法律体系边界都画出来的地图。

abstract.en: Think of a courtroom argument being sorted into rival schools of thought.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭上的一场辩论被分门别类归入几大思想流派。

examples.en: Jurisprudence asks what makes a rule a law.
examples.cn: 法理学追问的是：一条规则凭什么成为法律。

examples.en: The judge cited a long line of jurisprudence on privacy.
examples.cn: 这位法官援引了一长串有关隐私的判例。

examples.en: Students of jurisprudence compare how courts justify their rulings.
examples.cn: 研习法理学的学生比较各法院如何为自己的判决说理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「久瑞斯 普鲁登斯」——一位叫普鲁登斯的人把法律讲得很「审慎」，于是成了法理学；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ius / iur-（法律、权利）+ prudentia（知识、明智）→ iurisprudentia（法律知识）→ 古法语 jurisprudence → 英语 jurisprudence，核心义「懂法之智」。

sensesIntro.en: Jurisprudence begins as the learning that understands law, then widens to a national body of law, to rival legal theories, to judges case law, and finally to legal philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: jurisprudence 先是「懂法的学问」，随后扩展为一国的法律体系、彼此竞争的法律理论、法官积累的判例法，最后又成为法律哲学的代称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open law book beside a heap of case files.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本摊开的法典旁边堆着厚厚的判词卷宗。

branches.en: The core sense is the science of law.
branches.cn: 核心义项是研究法律的学问。

branches.en: A national system is the discipline applied to one country.
branches.cn: 一国的法律体系是这门学问落到具体国家的形态。

branches.en: A school of theory sets one reading of law against others.
branches.cn: 理论流派是把一种读法与其他读法对立起来。

branches.en: Case law is legal wisdom accumulated in actual rulings.
branches.cn: 判例法是法律智慧在实际判决中的积累。

branches.en: The academic discipline and legal philosophy share the same abstract question.
branches.cn: 学院学科与法律哲学共享同一个抽象问题：法律究竟是什么。

intro.en: Jurisprudence combines jur-, from ius, with the prudentia element, and the same pieces build jurist and jurisprudential.
intro.cn: jurisprudence 把来自 ius 的 jur- 与 prudentia 一类词尾组合起来，同样的构件也构成 jurist 与 jurisprudential。

latinIntro.en: Ius means law or right, prudentia means knowledge or prudence, and iurisprudentia fuses them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius 意为法律或权利，prudentia 意为知识、审慎，iurisprudentia 把两者合在一起。

items.example: Ius supplies the law element in the word.
items.exampleCN: ius 提供这个词中的「法律」成分。

items.example: The root iur- appears at the head of the word.
items.exampleCN: 词根 iur- 出现在词首。

items.example: Prudentia adds the wisdom component.
items.exampleCN: prudentia 加入「智慧」成分。

items.example: Iurisprudentia is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: iurisprudentia 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Juridical uses the same law root.
items.exampleCN: juridical 使用同一个「法律」词根。

items.meaning: the authority to hear a case
items.example: Jurisdiction joins ius to dicere, to say.
items.exampleCN: jurisdiction 把 ius 与 dicere（说）接在一起。

items.example: Jurist is the person who studies law.
items.exampleCN: jurist 是研究法律的人。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms jurisprudential.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成 jurisprudential。

items.example: Prudence keeps the second half of the word alive.
items.exampleCN: prudence 延续了词的后半部分。

items.example: Prudential shares the prudentia root.
items.exampleCN: prudential 共享 prudentia 词根。

definition_zh: 果核；仁；核心；要点；操作系统内核
definition_en: the inner seed of a nut or grain, and by extension the central, essential part of something
core_image: 一枚硬壳被敲开，里面露出可以发芽的那颗小小的仁
scene: 老人把核桃夹开，小心取出里面白白的一小团。The old man cracked the walnut and lifted out the pale kernel with a knife.
sceneCN: 这里 kernel 是「果仁、果核」（第 1 个义项：坚果或谷粒里面可发芽的种子）；句意：老人把核桃夹开，用刀挑出里面那团浅色的小仁。

pos.zh: 果仁；核心；要点；（操作系统）内核

collocations.zh: 内核崩溃（计算机系统故障）

collocations.phrase: at the kernel of the argument

derivatives.zh: 带核的；有仁的；构成名词 kernel 时加 -ed 表示「具有……的」
字母间距调整；与 kernel 拼写相近，但一般认为并非出自同一来源

senses.title: The soft seed inside a shell
senses.definition: the softer, edible, or seed-bearing part inside the hard shell of a nut or the coat of a grain
senses.definitionCN: 坚果硬壳内或谷粒外壳内较软、可食用或能发芽的部分
senses.example: She cracked open the shell and ate the kernel.
senses.exampleCN: 她敲开外壳，吃掉了里面的果仁。
senses.why: The oldest sense is physical: the small living seed hidden at the centre of a hard case, and that picture shapes every later meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是物理层面的：藏在硬壳正中、能发芽的那颗小种子；正是这幅画面决定了后来的所有引申义。

senses.title: A single grain of cereal
senses.definition: one whole grain of wheat, maize, or similar cereal
senses.definitionCN: 一颗完整的麦粒、玉米粒或类似谷物籽粒
senses.example: Each ear of maize carries hundreds of kernels.
senses.exampleCN: 每个玉米穗上有数百粒玉米。
senses.why: A grain is simply the kernel of a cereal plant, so the grain-crop sense is the same object seen from the field rather than the table.
senses.whyCN: 谷粒本来就是谷物这种植物的「仁」，所以这个谷物义项只是同一个东西从田间而不是从餐桌上被看到而已。

senses.title: The central essential part
senses.definition: the most important or essential part of something such as an idea, argument, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 想法、论点或计划等事物中最重要、最本质的部分
senses.example: Strip away the jargon and the kernel of the argument is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 去掉那些行话，这个论点的核心其实很简单。
senses.why: What is inside the shell is the valuable part, so a kernel becomes the part of a plan or argument that matters once the wrapping is removed.
senses.whyCN: 壳里那部分是真正有价值的东西，所以 kernel 就成了计划或论点「去掉包装后真正要紧的核心」。

senses.title: The core of an operating system
senses.definition: the central program of an operating system that manages memory, processes, and devices
senses.definitionCN: 管理计算机内存、进程与硬件设备的核心程序
senses.example: A bug in the kernel can freeze the whole machine.
senses.exampleCN: 内核里的一个缺陷就可能让整台机器卡死。
senses.why: Computing borrows the same image: the core of a system is the part every other program depends on, hidden beneath the surface.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了同一幅画面：系统的核心就是所有其他程序都依赖、却藏在表层之下的那一部分。

senses.title: A core of truth in a claim
senses.definition: a small but real element of truth inside a statement that is mostly wrong or exaggerated
senses.definitionCN: 大多错误或夸大的说法里，真实而有限的那一点成分
senses.example: Even the rumour had a kernel of truth.
senses.exampleCN: 就连那个谣言也有一点真实成分。
senses.why: If a statement is a shell of exaggeration, the kernel is the small piece of solid truth rattling inside it.
senses.whyCN: 如果说辞是一层夸张的外壳，那么 kernel 就是壳里那点实在的真话。

intro.en: Kernel comes from Old English cyrnel, a small seed, a diminutive of corn, the word for grain.
intro.cn: kernel 来自古英语 cyrnel，意为小种子，是表示谷物的 corn 的指小形式。

items.en: Cyrnel means a small seed or grain, formed from corn plus a small-suffix.
items.cn: cyrnel 意为小种子、谷粒，由 corn 加一个指小词尾构成。

items.en: The word appears as kirnel, naming the edible part inside a nut or fruit stone.
items.cn: 中古英语作 kirnel，指坚果或果核内可食用的部分。

items.en: The core image extends to the central part of a thing, as in the kernel of a plan.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，核心意象扩展到事物的中心部分，如计划的核心。

items.en: Some uses shift spelling toward kernel, matching the loss of the r sound in eastern England.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪，部分拼写转向 kernel，与英格兰东部 r 音弱化的发音习惯相合。

items.en: Computer scientists name the core program of an operating system a kernel in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，计算机科学家把操作系统的核心程序称为 kernel。

note.en: Kernel is easily confused with colonel, a military rank of different origin, and sits beside core, nucleus, and gist.
note.cn: kernel 容易与表示军衔的 colonel 混淆，而后者来源不同；它又与 core、nucleus、gist 义近。

entries.definition: a senior military officer; only spelling and sound are close, the source is different
entries.definitionCN: 上校（只是拼写和读音相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: grain in general, from which kernel is a diminutive
entries.definitionCN: 谷物；谷粒（kernel 由它加指小词尾构成）

entries.definition: relating to a nucleus; only the sound echoes kernel, with a different root
entries.definitionCN: 核的；原子核的（只是发音近似，词根不同）

entries.definition: the central part of something
entries.definitionCN: 核心；中心部分

entries.definition: the central structure around which others gather
entries.definitionCN: 核心；原子核；细胞核

entries.definition: the main point of what was said
entries.definitionCN: 要点；主旨

normalIntro.en: Kernel is the little corn inside the shell: a small cyrnel of grain or truth.
normalIntro.cn: kernel 就是壳里的那颗小谷物：一粒 cyrnel，既可以指谷仁，也可以指事实的内核。

normal.en: Cyrnel is corn plus a small-suffix, so kernel is literally a small grain.
normal.cn: cyrnel 是 corn 加指小词尾，所以 kernel 字面意思就是「小谷粒」。

normal.en: A kernel of truth is the real piece inside a doubtful story.
normal.cn: a kernel of truth 就是指可疑说法里那点真实内容。

normal.en: Corn kernel and palm kernel oil keep the grain sense alive in industry.
normal.cn: corn kernel 与 palm kernel oil 让「谷粒」义项在工业用语中延续下来。

normal.en: Compare colonel: same sound, different origin and meaning.
normal.cn: 对比 colonel：读音相同，来源与含义都不同。

normal.en: Core and kernel share the image, but kernel keeps the seed-in-a-shell picture.
normal.cn: core 与 kernel 共享核心意象，但 kernel 保留了「壳中之仁」的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a walnut shell cracking open to show one white seed.
abstract.cn: 想象胡桃壳裂开，露出一颗白色的仁。

abstract.en: Imagine a long speech folded into a single sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇长演讲被折成一句话。

abstract.en: Think of an operating system as a tree with one trunk holding every branch.
abstract.cn: 把操作系统想成一棵树：主干支撑全部枝杈。

examples.en: Roast the kernels and sprinkle them on the salad.
examples.cn: 把果仁烤一下，撒在沙拉上。

examples.en: There is a kernel of truth in what she said.
examples.cn: 她说的话里有一点真实成分。

examples.en: The kernel of the proposal is to work together rather than compete.
examples.cn: 这份提案的核心是合作而非竞争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「壳哪儿」——壳哪里去了？敲开壳，才看见里面那颗小小的「仁」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 corn（谷物）+ 指小词尾 -el → cyrnel（小谷粒）→ 中古英语 kirnel → 现代英语 kernel，核心义「壳中之仁」。

sensesIntro.en: Kernel starts as the seed inside a shell, then covers a single grain, then the essential part of anything, with computer use as a late technical branch.
sensesIntro.cn: kernel 从「壳里的种子」出发，再到单粒谷物，再到任何事物的核心要点，最后分化出计算机术语这一技术分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard shell cracked open around one pale seed.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳被敲开，露出里面那颗浅色的小仁。

branches.en: The seed inside a nut is the physical source.
branches.cn: 坚果壳里的仁是物理来源。

branches.en: One cereal grain is that seed seen in the field.
branches.cn: 一粒谷物就是田间看到的同一颗种子。

branches.en: The central part of an idea follows the peel-it-away image.
branches.cn: 想法的核心延续了「剥去外壳」的意象。

branches.en: An operating system kernel is the technical heir of the same centre.
branches.cn: 操作系统内核是同一「中心」概念的技术继承者。

branches.en: The kernel of an argument and a kernel of truth both name the solid part.
branches.cn: 论点的核心与说法中的真实成分都指那个结实的内核。

intro.en: Kernel has no Latin affixes: it is native English, built from corn with a small suffix, and it later takes ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: kernel 没有拉丁词缀，它是本土英语词，由 corn 加指小词尾构成，之后只接英语常用词尾。

latinIntro.en: Kernel is of Germanic origin, so no Latin entry is really a cognate, and none is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: kernel 属日耳曼语源，没有真正意义上的拉丁同源词，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

items.example: Corn is the base of the word.
items.exampleCN: corn 是这个单词的基础。

items.example: The suffix -el makes corn into a small seed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -el 把 corn 变成「小种子」。

items.example: Cyrnel is the oldest recorded shape.
items.exampleCN: cyrnel 是有记录的最早形态。

items.example: Kirnel names the edible nut flesh.
items.exampleCN: kirnel 指坚果里可食用的部分。

items.example: Kernel carries both senses today.
items.exampleCN: kernel 今天同时承载这两种含义。

items.example: The plural suffix -s gives kernels.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾 -s 构成 kernels。

items.meaning: core program of an operating system
items.example: Computing reuses the small-word image for software.
items.exampleCN: 计算机领域把「内核画面」借给了软件。

items.meaning: a kernel that tastes bitter and is toxic raw
items.example: Bitter kernel names the almond variety used in flavouring.
items.exampleCN: bitter kernel 指用于调味的那种苦杏仁。

definition_zh: 拱顶石；基石；关键；支柱
definition_en: the central stone at the top of an arch, and by extension the part on which everything else depends
core_image: 一圈石块围成拱门，最顶端那块楔形石严丝合缝地卡住整圈
scene: 工人把最后一块石头吊到拱门顶端，整座桥才真正稳住了。Once the keystone was set, the whole arch finally held its shape.
sceneCN: 这里 keystone 是「拱顶石」（第 1 个义项：拱门顶端正中的那块楔形石）；句意：拱顶石一放好，整个拱门才终于稳住形状。

pos.zh: 拱顶石；基石；关键；支柱

collocations.zh: 关键习惯（带动全局的习惯）

derivatives.zh: 砌有拱顶石的；构成名词 keystone 时加 -ed 表示「具有……的」
关键的；最重要的，与 keystone 共用一个前部，但并非由它派生

senses.title: The stone at the top of an arch
senses.definition: the central wedge-shaped stone at the highest point of an arch that locks the other stones in place
senses.definitionCN: 拱门最高处正中的楔形石块，锁住其余石块的位置
senses.example: The stonemason lowered the keystone into the gap at the top.
senses.exampleCN: 石匠把拱顶石放到顶部缺口里。
senses.why: The literal image is architectural: a single wedge at the crown that presses every other stone outward and keeps them from falling.
senses.whyCN: 这个字面意象来自建筑：顶端一块楔石向两侧外推，把其他石块压住，使它们不至于塌落。

senses.title: The stone at the base of a corner
senses.definition: the large stone at the base of a wall corner, on which later courses are laid
senses.definitionCN: 墙角的底座大石，上面的砖石层层砌在它之上
senses.example: The old bank still shows its carved keystone on the street corner.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旧银行街角上仍露出雕花的墙角基石。
senses.why: The word can mark whichever stone carries the structure, at the crown of an arch or at the foot of a corner wall.
senses.whyCN: 凡是承担整个结构的石块，词都可以用：既可以是拱顶，也可以是墙角底座。

senses.title: The part everything depends on
senses.definition: the essential element that holds together a system, argument, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 支撑起一个体系、论点或组织的关键要素
senses.example: Trust is the keystone of any long partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是任何长期合作关系的基石。
senses.why: If a stone holds an arch together, then whatever holds a system together inherits the name, so the metaphor moves from stone to idea.
senses.whyCN: 既然一块石头能撑住拱门，那么撑住任何体系的要素自然也继承了这个名字，比喻便从石头搬到思想上。

senses.title: A species that holds an ecosystem
senses.definition: a species whose removal would cause many other species to disappear
senses.definitionCN: 一旦消失就会导致许多其他物种随之消亡的物种
senses.example: Sea otters are a keystone in coastal kelp forests.
senses.exampleCN: 海獭是沿海海藻林里的关键物种。
senses.why: Ecology takes the architectural image literally: one species wedges the whole system in place, just as one stone holds the arch.
senses.whyCN: 生态学直接沿用建筑画面：一个物种像楔石那样把整个系统卡住，正如一块石头撑住拱门。

senses.title: A puzzle answer check
senses.definition: an old name for the check word printed with a puzzle answer to verify a solver response
senses.definitionCN: 旧时谜题答案旁印的核验字，用来核对读者的解答是否正确
senses.example: Old puzzle books printed a keystone beside the answer.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时谜题书会在答案旁印一个核验字。
senses.why: Publishers borrowed the stone image for the small fact that confirms the whole answer is correctly assembled.
senses.whyCN: 出版者借用了石头意象：一个小小的核验字，用来确认整个答案拼装正确。

intro.en: Keystone is a straightforward English compound of key and stone, with key here meaning the stone that locks an arch.
intro.cn: keystone 是英语里直接的复合词，由 key 与 stone 组成，这里的 key 指「锁住拱门的石头」。

items.en: Stān is the native word for stone, and cǣg names a key.
items.cn: stān 是本土表示石头的词，cǣg 表示钥匙。

items.en: Key grows a building sense: the stone that closes and locks a vault or arch.
items.cn: 中古英语里 key 发展出建筑含义：封闭并锁住拱顶的那块石头。

items.en: The compound keystone is recorded for the top stone of an arch.
items.cn: 十六世纪有记录 keystone 指拱门顶端的石头。

items.en: The figurative use, the keystone of a system, spreads in political and religious writing.
items.cn: 十九世纪，比喻用法「体系的基石」在政治与宗教写作中流行。

items.en: Ecology coins keystone species, and American usage adds state nicknames such as the Keystone State.
items.cn: 现代英语中生态学造出 keystone species，美国用法又增添宾夕法尼亚州「拱心石州」之类的别称。

note.en: Keystone is built from key plus stone and stands beside foundation, cornerstone, and pillar as a metaphor for indispensable support.
note.cn: keystone 由 key 与 stone 合成，与 foundation、cornerstone、pillar 一起构成「不可或缺的支撑」这一比喻群。

entries.definition: a small metal tool that opens a lock, or the essential thing itself
entries.definitionCN: 钥匙；也可指关键物（与 keystone 共享 key 部分）

entries.definition: hard mineral matter used in building
entries.definitionCN: 石头；建筑用石材（复合词的后半）

entries.definition: a marker stone, or an important event; shares only the stone head, with a different image
entries.definitionCN: 里程碑；重要事件（只共享 stone 部分，意象不同）

entries.definition: the base on which something is built
entries.definitionCN: 地基；基础

entries.definition: a stone at the corner of a building on which later work depends
entries.definitionCN: 墙角石；奠基石

entries.definition: a tall supporting column, or a key member of a group
entries.definitionCN: 柱子；栋梁；中坚

normalIntro.en: Keystone is the key stone: the one stone that locks the others in place.
normalIntro.cn: keystone 就是「钥匙石」：那把把其他石头锁住的关键石。

normal.en: Key plus stone explains the word literallly: a stone that locks.
normal.cn: key 加 stone 直接解释了造词：一把能上锁的石头。

normal.en: Pull the keystone out and the arch falls, so it is the key element.
normal.cn: 把拱顶石抽掉，拱门就塌了，所以它是关键要素。

normal.en: Keystone species keeps the ecological image of the stone.
normal.cn: keystone species 保留了那块石头的生态学画面。

normal.en: Compare cornerstone: one sits at the top of an arch, the other at a corner foundation.
normal.cn: 对比 cornerstone：一个坐在拱顶，一个埋在墙角地基。

normal.en: Pennsylvania is nicknamed the Keystone State for its central place in the colonies.
normal.cn: 宾夕法尼亚州别称拱心石州，因为它在早期殖民地中居中枢之位。

abstract.en: Picture a child pulling the top stone from a wall of blocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子从积木墙里抽出最顶上那块石头。

abstract.en: Think of one word that suddenly makes a whole paragraph clear.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词突然让整段话豁然开朗。

abstract.en: Imagine a forest dying after one animal is hunted out.
abstract.cn: 想象一种动物被捕杀殆尽后，整片森林随之衰败。

examples.en: Each keystone is cut larger at the top than at the bottom.
examples.cn: 每块拱顶石上宽下窄。

examples.en: Education is the keystone of a fair society.
examples.cn: 教育是公平社会的基石。

examples.en: Remove a keystone species and the food web collapses.
examples.cn: 去掉一个关键物种，食物网就会崩溃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「key stone」——拱门用了它才算「上锁」，一看就是关键的那块石头；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 cǣg（钥匙）+ stān（石头）→ 中古英语 key 的「锁拱之石」义 + stone → 英语 keystone（拱顶石）→ 引申为「基石、关键」。

sensesIntro.en: Keystone begins with the stone that locks an arch in place, extends to a corner base stone, and then moves from stone to idea as the indispensable part of any system.
sensesIntro.cn: keystone 从「锁住拱门的那块石头」出发，延伸到墙角基石，再由石头转向思想，指任何体系中不可或缺的关键部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one wedge stone pressing the arch into a stable curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块楔石把拱门压成稳定的弧线。

branches.en: The arch crown stone is the literal origin.
branches.cn: 拱顶石是字面来源。

branches.en: A corner base stone is the same carrier seen from the foot of the wall.
branches.cn: 墙角基石是同一个「承载者」从墙脚看过去的样子。

branches.en: An essential part of a system is the metaphor fully transferred.
branches.cn: 体系中的关键部分是比喻完全迁移后的结果。

branches.en: A keystone species applies the metaphor to living things.
branches.cn: 关键物种把这个比喻用到了生物身上。

branches.en: A lock stone and a check word both keep something from falling apart.
branches.cn: 锁石与核验字都是防止整体散掉的那一环。

intro.en: Keystone is a native compound, so the useful pieces are Germanic free words rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: keystone 是本土复合词，真正有用的是日耳曼语系的自由词根，而不是拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: Both halves of keystone descend from Old English, so there is no Latin cognate to list here.
latinIntro.cn: keystone 的两半都来自古英语，没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.example: Stone is the head that the compound modifies.
items.exampleCN: stone 是被修饰的中心词。

items.example: Keystone is recorded in English by the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: keystone 在十六世纪已见于英语。

items.example: The plural suffix -s gives keystones.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾 -s 构成 keystones。

items.meaning: a species on which an ecosystem depends
items.meaningCN: 生态系统赖以维系的关键物种
items.example: Ecology uses the compound phrase for ecosystem anchors.
items.exampleCN: 生态学用这个复合短语表示生态系统的锚。

items.meaning: the base stone of a corner
items.example: Cornerstone builds the same metaphor with corner.
items.exampleCN: cornerstone 用 corner 构成同一比喻。

items.meaning: a marker stone, an important event
items.example: Milestone shares the stone head with a different image.
items.exampleCN: milestone 与它共享 stone，但意象不同。

items.meaning: a coping stone on top of a wall
items.meaningCN: 墙顶压顶石；成就的顶点
items.example: Capstone plays the same role for flat walls.
items.exampleCN: capstone 在平顶墙上扮演同样的角色。

items.meaningCN: 美国宾夕法尼亚州的别称
items.example: The state nickname extends the central image.
items.exampleCN: 州别称延伸了「居中关键」的意象。

items.example: Key alone carries the adjective idea today.
items.exampleCN: 如今 key 单独就能表示「关键的」。

definition_zh: 点燃；点着；激起；唤起；燃起
definition_en: to start a fire or make something catch light, and by extension to stir up a feeling or an interest
core_image: 一颗火星落在干柴上，先冒出一点火光，随后整堆柴燃起
scene: 冬夜壁炉里只剩一点余烬，小屋冷得让人发抖。She bent down and used a twist of dry paper to kindle the damp logs again.
sceneCN: 这里 kindle 是「点燃、引燃」（第 1 个义项：使柴薪等起火）；句意：她弯下腰，用一小撮干纸把潮了的木柴重新引着。

pos.zh: 点燃；引燃；激起；唤起
着火；燃起

derivatives.zh: 引火物；点火的细柴
重新点燃；重新激起
点火的人；引起者（较少用）

senses.title: To set something on fire
senses.definition: to make wood, paper or other material start to burn
senses.definitionCN: 使木头、纸张或其他材料开始燃烧
senses.example: A single match was enough to kindle the dry grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一根火柴就足以点着干草。
senses.why: The Old Norse verb kynda meant to light a fire or a lamp, and that fire-making image is the root of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语动词 kynda 意为「点灯、生火」，生火这个画面是后来所有义项的源头。

senses.title: To stir up a feeling
senses.definition: to arouse a strong feeling such as hope, enthusiasm or love in someone
senses.definitionCN: 唤起希望、热情或爱这类强烈情感
senses.example: Her speech kindled hope in the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 她的讲话在整座村子唤起了希望。
senses.why: A feeling spreads the way fire does, from a small spark to a whole blaze, so kindling hope keeps the original fire image.
senses.whyCN: 情感像火一样蔓延，从一点火星烧成一片大火，所以「点燃希望」仍保留着原来的火焰意象。

senses.title: To start someone doing something
senses.definition: to make someone begin to feel interest in something or become active about it
senses.definitionCN: 使人对某事产生兴趣或开始采取行动
senses.example: A single school visit kindled her love of science.
senses.exampleCN: 一次学校参观引起了她对科学的热爱。
senses.why: Interest is treated as a flame that a teacher or a book can set alight in a learner.
senses.whyCN: 兴趣被看成可以被老师或一本书在学习者身上点着的一团火。

senses.title: To cause a dispute to flare up
senses.definition: to cause a debate, controversy or conflict to begin or to grow stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使争论、争议或冲突开始或加剧
senses.example: The new tax rules have kindled a fierce argument among shop owners.
senses.exampleCN: 新的税收规定在店主中引发了一场激烈的争论。
senses.why: A public argument spreads like a fire in dry wind, so the same verb is used for starting conflict.
senses.whyCN: 公开的争论像干风里的火一样蔓延，所以同一个动词也用来表示挑起冲突。

senses.title: To become lit
senses.definition: used without an object, of something showing itself and starting to burn or light up
senses.definitionCN: 作不及物动词，指某物显现并开始燃烧或亮起
senses.example: In the story the first stars kindle above the snowy field.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，最初几颗星星在雪原上空亮了起来。
senses.why: Some writers use kindle without an object, as if fire appeared on its own, which is the intransitive branch of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 一些作者把 kindle 用作不及物动词，仿佛火自己冒出来，这是同一意象的不及物分支。

intro.en: Kindle comes from Old Norse kynda, to light a fire, and possibly from an older root meaning a torch.
intro.cn: kindle 来自古诺斯语 kynda（生火、点着），更早一般认为与表示「火炬」的词干有关。

items.en: The reconstructed form kwenþjan means to set alight, and it may relate to the word for a torch.
items.cn: 据重构，原始日耳曼语形式 kwenþjan 意为「点着」，一般认为与「火炬」一词相关。

items.en: Kynda means to light a fire, a candle or a lamp.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kynda 意为点起篝火、蜡烛或灯。

items.en: The verb appears in English as cundel, tyndel and later kindle, borrowed from the Norse settlers.
items.cn: 该动词在十二世纪以 cundel、tyndel 等形式进入英语，后来写成 kindle，一般认为借自北欧移民。

items.en: The sense widens from lighting a fire to arousing feelings.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，词义从点火扩展到激起情感。

items.en: Kindle supplies the noun kindling, the verb rekindle and a range of figurative uses.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，kindle 派生出名词 kindling、动词 rekindle，并发展出大量比喻用法。

note.en: Kindle is the Norse fire verb, close to kindling, rekindle and ignite, and to the near meanings ignite and light.
note.cn: kindle 是源自北欧语的「点火」动词，与 kindling、rekindle、ignite 同族，与 ignite、light 意义相近。

entries.definition: small dry sticks or material used to start a fire
entries.definitionCN: 引火的细柴或材料

entries.definition: to light something again or to stir a feeling up again
entries.definitionCN: 重新点燃；重新激起

entries.definition: royal or noble, related to a king
entries.definitionCN: 国王的；威严的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to make something burn, often suddenly or with force
entries.definitionCN: 点燃；燃烧（常指猛然起火）

entries.definition: to make something start to burn
entries.definitionCN: 点着；生火

entries.definition: to cause something to start, especially a strong feeling
entries.definitionCN: 触发；引发（尤指情感）

normalIntro.en: Kindle is a small flame handed over from an older torch word: light the dry material and the whole fire follows.
normalIntro.cn: kindle 是承袭自古雅语「火炬」词的一小簇火苗：点着干燥的引火物，整堆火就会跟着烧起来。

normal.en: Kindle a fire means start a fire, often with small dry things first.
normal.cn: kindle a fire 指生火，通常先点着干燥的引火物。

normal.en: Kindling is the small wood you use at the start.
normal.cn: kindling 就是一开始用来引火的细柴。

normal.en: The prefix re- turns kindle into rekindle, to light again.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 把 kindle 变成 rekindle，表示重新点燃。

normal.en: Kindle hope and kindle interest use the fire image for feelings.
normal.cn: kindle hope 与 kindle interest 都用火焰意象表示情感。

normal.en: Compare ignite: ignite is more technical and often sudden, kindle is gentler and often figurative.
normal.cn: 对比 ignite：ignite 更技术化、常指骤然起火，kindle 更温和、更常用于比喻。

abstract.en: Picture a spark on a dry bundle of sticks, then the whole heap in flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火星落在干草束上，整堆柴随即烧起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher passing a small flame of curiosity to a pupil.
abstract.cn: 想象老师把一小簇好奇的火苗交给学生。

abstract.en: Think of a match being struck, and the interest that follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一根火柴被划亮，随之而来的是被点起的兴趣。

examples.en: The campers kindled a small fire with dry twigs.
examples.cn: 露营者用干树枝生起了一小堆火。

examples.en: The documentary kindled public interest in local wildlife.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片激起了公众对本地野生动物的兴趣。

examples.en: The discovery kindled hopes for an early cure.
examples.cn: 这一发现燃起了早日找到疗法的希望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「亲抖」——火柴一点，手亲亲地一抖，火苗就冒出来了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺斯语 kynda（生火、点着）→ 中古英语 cundel、tyndel → kindle，核心义「点着火苗」。

sensesIntro.en: Kindle starts with lighting a fire, then moves the same spark to feelings, to a learner taking interest, to public disputes and to things lighting up on their own.
sensesIntro.cn: kindle 先指点火，再把同一点火花移到情感的燃起、学习者兴趣的产生、公共争论的引发，以及事物自行亮起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spark on dry kindling, then the whole fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一点火星落在干柴上，随后整堆火燃起。

branches.en: A concrete fire is the everyday sense and the base of the map.
branches.cn: 真实的火是日常义项，也是整张语义图的基础。

branches.en: Feelings such as hope and love are treated as flames that someone can light.
branches.cn: 希望、爱这类情感被当作可被他人点着的火焰。

branches.en: Interest is a flame a teacher or a book can set alight in a learner.
branches.cn: 兴趣是老师或一本书能在学习者身上点燃的火苗。

branches.en: A debate spreads like fire in dry wind, so kindle also starts conflict.
branches.cn: 争论像干风里的火一样蔓延，所以 kindle 也能挑起冲突。

branches.en: The fire itself can kindle, with no one holding the match.
branches.cn: 火本身也能 kindle，无需有人拿着火柴。

intro.en: Kindle is a Norse loan verb with a small English family: kindling, rekindle and the rarer kindler.
intro.cn: kindle 是来自古诺斯语的借词，英语中的词族不大，包括 kindling、rekindle 以及较少用的 kindler。

latinIntro.en: Kindle has no Latin origin, so the Latin relatives listed here are only loose cousins from fire words.
latinIntro.cn: kindle 并非源自拉丁语，这里列出的拉丁词只是「火」义场的远亲，不是同源词。

definition_zh: 诀窍；天赋；技巧；本领
definition_en: an unusual ability to do a particular thing well, often one that seems natural rather than learned
core_image: 手指在绳结上一拨，结就自己松开了，旁人却拉了半天也解不开
scene: 培训课上，新来的学徒反复练同一个结，总是越拉越紧。The old ranger soon showed a real knack for tying the knots that hold a shelter against wind.
sceneCN: 这里 knack 是「诀窍、熟练的技能」（第 1 个义项：把某事做好的特别本领）；句意：那位老护林员很快显露出把搭建帐篷防风所需的绳结打好的真本领。

pos.zh: 诀窍；技艺；天赋；习惯（常用于 have a knack of doing）

collocations.zh: 有做某事的本事（常指惹人注意的本事）

derivatives.zh: 筋疲力尽的（英式口语，一般认为与 knack 无关）
机巧的；灵巧的（方言与古旧用法）

senses.title: A special skill
senses.definition: a clever and practised way of doing something well that is hard to explain to others
senses.definitionCN: 把某事做好的一种巧妙而熟练的方法，却很难向别人讲清楚
senses.example: He has the knack of putting anxious travellers at ease.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一种让焦虑的旅客放松下来的诀窍。
senses.why: The word first named a sharp noise or a smart trick, and a knack is still the small trick that makes a hard job easy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指清脆的声响或巧妙的小把戏，而 knack 至今仍是让难事变容易的那个小窍门。

senses.title: A natural talent
senses.definition: an ability someone seems to have from birth rather than by training
senses.definitionCN: 某人仿佛生来就有的、而非训练得来的能力
senses.example: She has a knack for remembering names and faces.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生就善于记住名字和面孔。
senses.why: What comes easily is felt as a gift of nature, so the sight of someone doing it without effort reinforces the talent sense.
senses.whyCN: 容易上手的东西让人觉得是天赋，看到某人不费力就做到，更强化了「天赋」这一义项。

senses.title: A trick of the trade
senses.definition: a practical trick or piece of know-how that people in a particular job learn over time
senses.definitionCN: 某一行业的人长期摸索出的实用技巧或门道
senses.example: Every baker has a private knack for judging when the dough is ready.
senses.exampleCN: 每位面包师都有自己判断面团是否揉好的窍门。
senses.why: The trick sense of the word suits the small tricks a craft teaches, which are passed on by watching rather than by writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的「小把戏」含义正好配得上手艺中的小窍门，它们靠观察而不是文字传下来。

senses.title: A puzzling habit
senses.definition: used in the pattern have a knack of doing, for something someone does constantly and oddly
senses.definitionCN: 用于 have a knack of doing 结构，指某人不断做出、令人费解的行为
senses.example: The new machine has a knack of stopping at the worst moment.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新机器总爱在最糟糕的时候停下来。
senses.why: When a thing seems to do something too often to be chance, people say it has a knack for it, as if the object had learned a bad habit.
senses.whyCN: 当某物做某事频繁得不像偶然，人们就说它有这个「本领」，仿佛这件东西养成了一个坏习惯。

intro.en: Knack probably comes from the Middle English cnak, a sharp knock or crack, and the sense of a clever device grew out of that.
intro.cn: knack 一般认为来自中古英语 cnak（清脆的敲击声、啪的一响），「巧妙的门道」这一含义由此发展而来。

items.en: Cnak names a sharp snap or crack, a sound of something striking hard.
items.cn: 中古英语 cnak 指清脆的啪响，是硬物相击的声音。

items.en: The word extends to a smart stroke, a trick or a device that makes a noise.
items.cn: 词义扩展到巧妙的一击、小把戏，以及能发出声响的机巧装置。

items.en: A knack means a clever way of doing something, the trick behind a result.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，knack 指做成某事的巧妙方法，即结果背后的小把戏。

items.en: The verb knick-knack and the phrase a knack of doing push the sense towards skill.
items.cn: 拟声的 knick-knack 与 a knack of doing 之类的说法，把词义推向「技能」。

items.en: Modern usage centres on a knack for something, an easy and often natural skill.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在 a knack for something，指轻松、常带天生意味的技能。

note.en: Knack is a small-trick noun, close to its sound relatives knick-knack and nick, and to the near meanings skill, talent and trick.
note.cn: knack 是表示「小窍门」的名词，与拟声同胞 knick-knack、nick 相邻，与 skill、talent、trick 意义相近。

entries.definition: a small decorative object of little value
entries.definitionCN: 不值钱的小装饰品；小玩意儿

entries.definition: to hit something, or the sound of hitting
entries.definitionCN: 敲；击打声（与 knack 拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a small cut, or to make a small cut
entries.definitionCN: 小切口；刻痕（与 knack 拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: an ability gained through training and practice
entries.definitionCN: 训练与练习获得的能力

entries.definition: a natural ability to do something well
entries.definitionCN: 天生的才能

entries.definition: an effective way of doing something, or a clever act
entries.definitionCN: 有效的办法；小把戏

normalIntro.en: Knack began as a sharp snap of sound, and the little trick behind that snap became a skill.
normalIntro.cn: knack 起初是清脆的一响，而这一响背后的巧劲后来成了技能。

normal.en: Have a knack for means be naturally good at something.
normal.cn: have a knack for 表示天生擅长某事。

normal.en: Have a knack of doing often describes a funny or annoying habit.
normal.cn: have a knack of doing 常描述有趣或恼人的习惯。

normal.en: Learn the knack of the trade means pick up the craft tricks.
normal.cn: 学会「行业诀窍」这一说法，就是掌握本行的门道。

normal.en: Lose the knack means you no longer do it easily.
normal.cn: lose the knack 表示你不再轻松做得到。

normal.en: Compare skill: skill can be measured and taught, a knack is smaller, quicker and often unteachable.
normal.cn: 对比 skill：技能可衡量、可传授，knack 更小、更灵巧，且常常难以言传。

abstract.en: Picture a finger flicking a tight knot and it opens at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在紧绳结上一拨，结立刻松开。

abstract.en: Imagine a child who can hear a tune once and hum it whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只听过一遍就能哼出整首曲子的孩子。

abstract.en: Think of a baker tapping the dough and knowing it is ready.
abstract.cn: 想象面包师敲一敲面团，就知道它可以了。

examples.en: She has a knack for making dull lessons lively.
examples.cn: 她很有一套把枯燥的课讲活的本事。

examples.en: It took me weeks to get the knack of riding a bike.
examples.cn: 我花了好几周才掌握骑自行车的窍门。

examples.en: He has lost the knack of listening after years of rushing.
examples.cn: 匆忙了多年之后，他丢掉了静心倾听的本事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捏克」——手指一捏一点，难题就被攻克，这就是诀窍；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 cnak（清脆的敲击声）→ 巧妙的一击、小把戏 → knack（诀窍、技能），核心义「巧劲」。

sensesIntro.en: Knack moves from a clever little trick to a skill, to an inborn gift, to craft know-how and finally to an odd habit a thing or a person keeps showing.
sensesIntro.cn: knack 从巧妙的小窍门走向技能，再走向天赋，然后是行业门道，最后指人或物反复表现出的古怪习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flick of a finger that opens a knot nobody else can untie.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指轻巧一拨，解开了别人怎么也解不开的结。

branches.en: The main sense keeps the small trick that makes a hard job easy.
branches.cn: 主要义项保留了让难事变容易的小窍门。

branches.en: What is done with ease is read as a gift of nature.
branches.cn: 做得轻松的本事被理解为天赋。

branches.en: A craft passes its tricks by watching, so a knack is trade know-how.
branches.cn: 手艺靠观察传承窍门，所以 knack 是行业门道。

branches.en: Both a personal knack and a craft trick save effort through a small right move.
branches.cn: 个人诀窍与行业窍门都靠一个小小的恰当动作省力。

branches.en: A knack can be a gift or a bad habit, since both show up without being taught.
branches.cn: knack 既可以是天赋也可以是坏习惯，因为两者都不必教就出现。

intro.en: Knack is a short English noun with no productive affixes, and its few relatives are mostly dialect words.
intro.cn: knack 是简短的英语名词，没有能产的词缀，它的少量亲缘词多为方言。

latinIntro.en: Knack has no Latin root, so the entries here are only parallel ideas from Latin, not cognates.
latinIntro.cn: knack 没有拉丁词根，这里列出的拉丁词只是意义平行的表达，并非同源词。

items.example: Cnak is the earliest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: cnak 是最早记录的形式。

items.example: Knack keeps the trick sense.
items.exampleCN: knack 保留了「窍门」的含义。

items.meaning: used before the thing the skill concerns
items.meaningCN: 引出技能所针对的对象
items.example: A knack for numbers is the usual pattern.
items.exampleCN: a knack for numbers 是常见结构。

items.meaning: used before the action in have a knack of doing
items.meaningCN: 在 have a knack of doing 中引出动作
items.example: He has a knack of forgetting his keys.
items.exampleCN: 他总有忘带钥匙的本事。

items.example: Knacks is the plural form.
items.exampleCN: knacks 是复数形式。

items.example: The suffix -y forms knacky.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 knacky。

items.example: Knacky survives in some dialects.
items.exampleCN: knacky 仍见于一些方言。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms knackered, a slang adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成俚语形容词 knackered。

items.example: Knackered is slang and of uncertain link to knack.
items.exampleCN: knackered 是俚语，与 knack 的关联说法不确定。

definition_zh: 背包；干粮袋；（徒步旅行用的）轻便背包
definition_en: a bag for carrying food and supplies on the back, strapped over both shoulders, especially when walking or travelling
core_image: 背在双肩上的一只帆布袋子，里面塞着干粮和换洗衣物
scene: 清晨的山道上，年轻人准备徒步走完全程，手里先掂了掂行李的分量。He packed bread, water and a folded map into his knapsack before the long climb.
sceneCN: 这里 knapsack 是「背包、干粮袋」（第 1 个义项：背在肩上的行囊）；句意：在长途登山之前，他把面包、水和一张折好的地图装进背包。

pos.zh: 背包；干粮袋；行囊

collocations.zh: 背包问题（计算机与数学术语）

derivatives.zh: 翻找；洗劫（第二部分同源，整体并非由背包义派生）
麻袋；大袋子（knapsack 的第二部分）

senses.title: A bag carried on the back
senses.definition: a bag with two shoulder straps, used for carrying things on the back
senses.definitionCN: 带两条肩带、用来背东西的袋子
senses.example: The hikers fastened their knapsacks and set off at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 徒步者系好背包，在黎明时出发。
senses.why: A knapsack is literally a bag of food, so it began as a bag of bread and water tied over the shoulders.
senses.whyCN: knapsack 字面上就是「装食物的袋子」，最初是一种装面包和水、系在肩上的袋子。

senses.title: Military field pack
senses.definition: the pack that soldiers wear on their backs to carry food, clothes and kit on the march
senses.definitionCN: 士兵行军时背在背上、装食物衣物和装备的包裹
senses.example: Each recruit was issued a rifle, a blanket and a knapsack.
senses.exampleCN: 每名新兵都配发了一支步枪、一条毯子和一个背囊。
senses.why: The word entered English through soldiers who needed a bag for the day, so the army sense has always been close to the middle of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是随需要携带日用品的士兵进入英语的，所以军用含义一直居于核心。

senses.title: Hiking pack
senses.definition: a simple light bag used by walkers and students to carry supplies for a trip
senses.definitionCN: 步行者或学生出门时装行李的轻便简易袋子
senses.example: A light knapsack is enough for a weekend on the trail.
senses.exampleCN: 在步道上过一个周末，一个轻便背包就够了。
senses.why: Once the pack left the army it lost its rations and kit, so the light walking bag is the same shape without the soldier weight.
senses.whyCN: 背包一旦离开军营，就不再装口粮和全套装具，于是轻便的徒步包成了同一种形状、却不带士兵负担的版本。

senses.title: Name of a computing problem
senses.definition: a classic problem in which objects of different value and weight must be chosen to fill a bag of fixed capacity
senses.definitionCN: 一个经典问题：在固定容量的袋子里挑选价值与重量各异的物品
senses.example: The knapsack problem is often used to teach simple algorithm design.
senses.exampleCN: 背包问题常被用来教授简单的算法设计。
senses.why: Researchers imagined a bag filled with valued items, took its old name and turned it into a standard puzzle in computing.
senses.whyCN: 研究者设想一只装有用价值物品的袋子，借用了这个旧名字，把它变成了计算机领域的标准难题。

intro.en: Knapsack joins German knappen, to eat, with sack, a bag, and reached English through soldiers in the Thirty Years War.
intro.cn: knapsack 由德语 knappen（吃）与不列颠拉丁语 saccus（袋子）构成，经三十年战争中的士兵传进英语。

items.en: Saccus, a bag, comes from Greek sakkos, and passes into English as sack.
items.cn: 拉丁语 saccus（袋子）源自希腊语 sakkos，后来以 sack 的形式进入英语。

items.en: Low German knappsack means a bag for food, from knappen, to eat or to snap up food.
items.cn: 十六世纪低地德语 knappsack 指装食物的袋子，来自 knappen（吃、咬食）。

items.en: Knapsack enters English, recorded in the early 1600s, with an earlier variant knapshalter, a bag carried by a soldier.
items.cn: knapsack 在十七世纪初进入英语，更早的变体 knapshalter 指士兵背的袋子。

items.en: Army usage fixes the word to a soldier pack worn on the back.
items.cn: 十八世纪的军中用法把这个词固定为士兵背在背上的行囊。

items.en: Hikers, students and later computer scientists borrow the word for everyday bags and a famous puzzle.
items.cn: 在现代英语中，徒步者、学生以及后来的计算机科学家借用这个词来表示日常背包和一个著名难题。

note.en: Knapsack is a German borrowed compound, close in form to ransack and sack, and close in meaning to rucksack, backpack and haversack.
note.cn: knapsack 是借自德语的复合词，形式上与 ransack、sack 相近，意义与 rucksack、backpack、haversack 相近。

entries.definition: to search a place roughly or to steal from it
entries.definitionCN: 翻找；洗劫（后段同源，前段来自房屋一词）

entries.definition: a large strong bag
entries.definitionCN: 大袋子；麻袋

entries.definition: to strike or knock sharply
entries.definitionCN: 猛击；敲打（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a bag worn on the back, especially for school or travel
entries.definitionCN: 背包；双肩包

entries.definition: a strong bag for walking, from German rucken and sack
entries.definitionCN: 登山背包（来自德语背与袋）

entries.definition: a small bag worn over one shoulder for food
entries.definitionCN: 单肩帆布口粮袋

normalIntro.en: Knapsack is a bag of food: knappen means to eat, and saccus means sack, so it is the bag you nibble from on the march.
normalIntro.cn: knapsack 是一只装食物的袋子：knappen 意为吃，saccus 意为袋，所以它是行军路上随时能伸手取食的那只包。

normal.en: Pack a knapsack before a hike means fill the bag with food and clothes.
normal.cn: pack a knapsack 指徒步前把食物和衣物装进包里。

normal.en: The knapsack problem is a standard puzzle about filling a bag well.
normal.cn: 背包问题是一个关于如何把袋子装得更好的经典难题。

normal.en: Rucksack shares the second part and the German origin.
normal.cn: rucksack 共享后段与德语来源。

normal.en: Ransack also contains the sack of knapsack.
normal.cn: ransack 也含有 knapsack 中的 sack。

normal.en: Compare backpack: backpack is the neutral everyday word, knapsack is older and slightly bookish.
normal.cn: 对比 backpack：backpack 是中性的日常词，knapsack 更老、略带书面气。

abstract.en: Picture a canvas bag bulging with bread and a tin cup on a soldier back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只帆布袋鼓鼓地装着面包和铁杯，背在士兵背上。

abstract.en: Imagine a recruit loaded with rifle, blanket and bag on a morning march.
abstract.cn: 想象一名新兵在晨间行军中背起步枪、毯子和行囊。

abstract.en: Think of a hiker checking a light bag before a weekend trail.
abstract.cn: 想象徒步者出发过周末前检查轻便背包。

examples.en: She filled her knapsack with apples and a bottle of water.
examples.cn: 她把背包塞满了苹果和一瓶水。

examples.en: Soldiers marched with knapsacks on their shoulders all day.
examples.cn: 士兵们背着行囊走了一整天。

examples.en: Every hiker should pack a knapsack light enough to carry uphill.
examples.cn: 每位徒步者都该把背包整理得轻到能背上坡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拿不散克」——背包拿不下、也散不开，只好一直背着；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 低地德语 knappen（吃）+ 拉丁语 saccus（袋子）→ 德语 knappsack（干粮袋）→ 英语 knapsack，核心义「背在肩上的食物袋」。

sensesIntro.en: Knapsack begins as a food bag, becomes a soldier pack and then a hiker bag, and finally lends its name to a computing puzzle.
sensesIntro.cn: knapsack 先是装食物的袋子，再成为士兵行囊与徒步背包，最后把自己的名字借给一个计算机难题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a canvas bag of bread and water slung over both shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着面包和水的帆布袋，斜挎在双肩上。

branches.en: The general bag for the back is the base sense of the map.
branches.cn: 泛指背在背上的袋子，是整张语义图的基础义。

branches.en: Army use is where the word spread, so the soldier pack is a major branch.
branches.cn: 军中用法是这个词扩散的源头，因此士兵行囊是重要分支。

branches.en: Walkers and students took the light version for trips.
branches.cn: 步行者和学生取用它的轻便版本出行。

branches.en: The everyday bag and the hiking bag differ only in size and weight.
branches.cn: 日常背包与徒步背包只在大小和重量上不同。

branches.en: The computing puzzle borrows the bag image for a capacity limit.
branches.cn: 计算机难题借用了袋子的意象来表示容量上限。

intro.en: Knapsack is a compound, with a German first part and a Latin-derived second part, and it has few productive affixes.
intro.cn: knapsack 是复合词，前段来自德语，后段源自拉丁语，本身缺少能产词缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin link is saccus, a bag, from Greek sakkos, which also gives English sack and ransack.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语关联在 saccus（袋子）与希腊语 sakkos，英语中的 sack 与 ransack 也出自这里。

items.exampleCN: knappen 提供了这个词「食物」的部分。

items.example: Knappsack is the direct German source.
items.exampleCN: knappsack 是直接的德语来源。

items.exampleCN: knapsacks 是复数形式。

definition_zh: 旋钮；球形把手；一小块（黄油等）；球形突起；门把手
definition_en: a rounded handle that you turn or pull, or a small round lump of something
core_image: 一只手捏住圆鼓鼓的把手，轻轻转动
scene: 老收音机侧面有一颗圆旋钮，转动它就能调大音量。She turned the round knob on the side of the old radio to make the music louder.
sceneCN: 这里 knob 是「旋钮」（第 1 个义项：需要转动或拉动的圆形把手）；句意：她转动旧收音机侧面的圆旋钮，把音乐调得更响。

pos.zh: 旋钮；球形把手；一小块（黄油等）；球形突起

由 knob 加 -ed 构成，义为「有球形把手的；带圆头的」
由 knob 加 -like 构成，义为「旋钮状的；球状的」

senses.title: A rounded control you turn
senses.definition: a round handle on a machine or device that you turn to control it
senses.definitionCN: 机器或设备上可转动以进行控制的圆形把手
senses.example: Turn the knob to the left to start the oven.
senses.exampleCN: 把旋钮向左转就能打开烤箱。
senses.why: The word names a rounded lump, and a round lump is exactly the shape of a control that the fingers grip and twist.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指圆鼓鼓的疙瘩，而疙瘩正好是手指能捏住并转动的控制件形状，于是引申为旋钮。

senses.title: A round door handle
senses.definition: a round piece of metal or wood on a door that you hold and turn to open it
senses.definitionCN: 门上供人握住并转动开门的圆形金属或木质件
senses.example: The door knob was loose and rattled every time.
senses.exampleCN: 门把手松了，每次都哗啦作响。
senses.why: From a control you grip, the sense widens to any round handle you grasp, and the door handle is the most common one.
senses.whyCN: 从手能握住的旋钮扩展到任何圆形的握持件，门上的球形把手是最常见的一种。

senses.title: A small lump of something
senses.definition: a small round piece of a soft substance, such as butter or cheese
senses.definitionCN: 黄油、奶酪等柔软物质的一小块
senses.example: Melt a knob of butter in the pan first.
senses.exampleCN: 先在锅里化一小块黄油。
senses.why: This keeps the oldest sense, a rounded lump, and the lump is small enough to sit on the end of a knife or spoon.
senses.whyCN: 这保留了最古老的含义，即圆块，而且这种小块刚好能放在刀尖或勺上。

senses.title: A rounded bump or swelling
senses.definition: a round swelling or protrusion on a surface or on a plant stem
senses.definitionCN: 表面或植物茎干上的圆形突起
senses.example: A hard knob had formed where the branch broke.
senses.exampleCN: 树枝折断的地方长出了一个硬结。
senses.why: The bare lump image also describes shapes in wood, bone, or soil, without any handle or control involved.
senses.whyCN: 光秃秃的圆块形象也能描述木头、骨头或泥土上的形状，此时与把手、控制完全无关。

senses.title: A dial or switch position
senses.definition: a marked position on a dial or switch that you set by turning
senses.definitionCN: 旋钮或开关上标出、通过转动选定的位置
senses.example: Set the thermostat on the highest knob for a quick bake.
senses.exampleCN: 把恒温器调到最高档以便快速烘烤。
senses.why: Since the knob is turned to choose, the marked positions it selects also take the same name in speech.
senses.whyCN: 因为旋钮是用来转着选择的，所以它选定并标出的那些档位在口语中也沿用同一个词。

senses.title: A knob of a hill or hilltop
senses.definition: a small rounded hill or the top of a hill
senses.definitionCN: 圆形的小山或山丘顶部
senses.example: We cycled up to the knob at the end of the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 我们骑车上到山脊尽头的那座小丘。
senses.why: A smooth round hill is a giant version of the same rounded lump, so the word widens from a hand-sized shape to a landscape.
senses.whyCN: 圆润的小山就是同一圆形疙瘩的巨大化版本，于是词义从手掌大小的形状扩展到山川地貌。

intro.en: Knob is a Middle English word for a rounded lump or a knot on a branch, probably of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: knob 是中古英语中表示「圆块」或「枝节」的词，一般认为源自日耳曼语。

items.en: A reconstructed root with a kn- sound seems to have named a lump, knot, or knuckle; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个以 kn- 开头、可能意为疙瘩、木节或指关节的重构词根被认为与此有关，确切形式存疑。

items.en: Knob first means a rounded lump, a knot in wood, or a swelling on a plant.
items.cn: knob 最早指圆形小块、木头上的节或植物上的突起。

items.en: A knob comes to be the rounded end of a handle, lever, or fitting.
items.cn: knob 开始指把手、杠杆或配件上圆形的端头。

items.en: Round door handles and cabinet handles are called knobs.
items.cn: 圆形的门把手与柜门把手都称为 knob。

items.en: Mechanical knobs on radios, cookers, and machines become the most familiar sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中，收音机、灶具和机器上的旋钮成为最熟悉的义项。

items.en: Informal British use adds a sense of a dull or annoying person, kept apart from the main senses here.
items.cn: 现代英式口语另有一个指「笨蛋、讨厌鬼」的义项，本词条不把它列入主要义项。

note.en: Knob is a round grip word, close in form to knock and in meaning to handle, bump, and hill.
note.cn: knob 是表示「圆形握持件」的词，形式上与 knock 相近，意义上与 handle、bump、hill 相邻。

entries.definition: to hit a door or surface with your hand
entries.definitionCN: 敲击；敲（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a fastening made by tying string, or a hard lump in wood
entries.definitionCN: 结；木节（同属 kn- 表示疙瘩或结的词，词源相近但不确定）

entries.definition: a joint in a finger, a rounded bump of bone
entries.definitionCN: 指关节（与 knob 同属「圆疙瘩」的意义圈，词源不同）

entries.definition: the part of an object you hold to use it
entries.definitionCN: 把手（泛指，不一定是圆形）

entries.definition: a round control with marks that you turn
entries.definitionCN: 刻度盘；表盘

entries.definition: a raised area on a flat surface
entries.definitionCN: 隆起；疙瘩

normalIntro.en: Knob is a round lump you can grip: it turns, it opens doors, and it sits on butter.
normalIntro.cn: knob 就是一个能握住的圆疙瘩：能转、能开门，还能放在黄油上。

normal.en: Turn the knob means rotate it to adjust a machine.
normal.cn: turn the knob 表示转动旋钮来调节机器。

normal.en: A door knob is the round handle you turn to open a door.
normal.cn: door knob 就是转一下就能开门的球形把手。

normal.en: A volume knob controls how loud the sound is.
normal.cn: volume knob 控制声音大小。

normal.en: A knob of butter is a small round portion of butter.
normal.cn: a knob of butter 就是一小块圆形黄油。

normal.en: Compare handle: handle is any grip, while knob is the round lump-shaped one.
normal.cn: 对比 handle：handle 是泛指握持件，knob 特指圆形疙瘩状的。

abstract.en: Picture two fingers pinching a round knob and twisting it slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象两根手指捏住圆旋钮，慢慢转动。

abstract.en: Imagine a brass door knob polished to a golden shine.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚擦得金光发亮的黄铜门把手。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny knob of butter melting at the edge of a hot pan.
abstract.cn: 想象热锅边上有一小块黄油慢慢化开。

examples.en: She turned the knob and pushed the door open.
examples.cn: 她转动把手，把门推开了。

examples.en: The knobs on the old radio were worn smooth.
examples.cn: 旧收音机上的旋钮被磨得光滑发亮。

examples.en: Add a knob of butter to the sauce before serving.
examples.cn: 上桌前往酱汁里加一小块黄油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捏宝」——手里捏着的圆疙瘩像宝贝，门把手上、机器上都是它；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 knob（圆块、木节），一般认为源自日耳曼语中表示「疙瘩、指节」的一族词（与 knot、knuckle 同属 kn- 词群，关系存疑）；核心义「圆鼓鼓的块状握持件」。

sensesIntro.en: Knob starts from a rounded lump, grows into round handles and controls, and keeps a lump sense for butter and for hills.
sensesIntro.cn: knob 从圆形疙瘩出发，发展为圆形把手与旋钮，同时保留「小块」义用于黄油和山丘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round grip in the fingers, ready to be turned.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指捏住圆鼓鼓的把手，随时可以转动。

branches.en: A control knob and the marked position it selects are two faces of the same turning.
branches.cn: 控制旋钮与它所选定的档位是同一「转动」动作的两面。

branches.en: The door knob is the everyday round handle sense.
branches.cn: 球形门把手是日常使用的圆形把手义项。

branches.en: A knob of butter keeps the oldest lump sense.
branches.cn: 一小块黄油保留了最古老的圆块义。

branches.en: A bump on a branch shows the lump image with no handle at all.
branches.cn: 树枝上的突起说明圆块形象完全不需要把手也能成立。

branches.en: Both a bump and a small hill are round rises in a larger surface.
branches.cn: 突起与小丘都是较大表面上圆鼓鼓的隆起。

intro.en: Knob is a native Germanic-style word with no Latin affix; its family grows with knobby, knobbed, and knoblike.
intro.cn: knob 是本土词，没有拉丁词缀，其词族依靠 knobby、knobbed 与 knoblike 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Knob has no Latin ancestor, so the Latin notes here only offer comparing forms such as nodus, a knot.
latinIntro.cn: knob 没有拉丁语祖先，这里仅列出 nodus（结）等可比形式供对照。

items.example: Knob is the base noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: knob 是这一词族的基础名词。

items.example: The plural knobs adds only -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数 knobs 只是加了 -s。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.meaningCN: 充满……的；具有……性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y turns knob into knobby.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 knob 变成 knobby。

items.example: Knobby knees have round bumps.
items.exampleCN: knobby knees 就是指膝盖有明显突起。

items.meaningCN: 具有所名词事物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms knobbed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 knobbed。

items.meaning: having a knob or round end
items.meaningCN: 有球形把手的；带圆头的
items.example: A knobbed stick has a round end.
items.exampleCN: a knobbed stick 指带圆头的手杖。

items.example: The suffix -like forms knoblike.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 knoblike。

items.example: Knoblike growths appear on the bark.
items.exampleCN: 树皮上会长出球状突起。

items.example: The phrase keeps the lump sense alive.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语让「圆块」义保持活跃。

items.example: The compound joins a round grip to a door.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词把圆形握持件与门连在一起。

latinEntries.example: Nodus is a comparing form only, not a source.
latinEntries.exampleCN: nodus 只是对照形式，并非来源。

latinEntries.example: Globus gives the round shape image.
latinEntries.exampleCN: globus 提供圆形球体的意象。

definition_zh: 棘手的；难解决的；多节的；缠绕纠结的
definition_en: difficult and complicated to solve, or full of knots
core_image: 一团绳子缠满死结，手指怎么拉也解不开
scene: 谈判桌上摆着一连串棘手的问题，谁都不愿先开口。The negotiators faced a knotty problem that no one wanted to discuss first.
sceneCN: 这里 knotty 是「棘手的」（第 1 个义项：复杂难解的问题）；句意：谈判者面对一个谁都不愿先开口讨论的棘手问题。

pos.zh: 棘手的；难解决的；多节的；纠结的

derivatives.zh: 由 knotty 去掉后缀 -y 得到的原词，义为「结；疙瘩」
由 knot 转成动词，义为「打结；缠结」
由 knotty 加 -ness 构成，义为「棘手；盘根错节的性质」
由 knot 加 -less 构成，义为「无结的；无节的」

senses.title: Difficult to solve
senses.definition: complex and hard to deal with, said of problems, issues, or questions
senses.definitionCN: 复杂难办的，用于形容问题、议题或疑问
senses.example: The team spent weeks on a knotty legal question.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小组花了好几周研究一个棘手的法律问题。
senses.why: A problem that will not come apart feels like string full of knots, so knotty moves from rope to reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 解不开的问题就像缠满结的绳子，于是 knotty 从绳索借用到思维与讨论中。

senses.title: Full of knots in wood
senses.definition: having many hard round knots in the wood or in a plant
senses.definitionCN: 木头或植物上有许多硬结的
senses.example: Knotty pine is cheap but hard to carve.
senses.exampleCN: 多节松木便宜，却很难雕刻。
senses.why: The suffix -y simply means full of, so the literal sense is wood full of knots, which is still the base picture.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 就是「充满」的意思，所以字面义是布满木节的木头，这仍是最基本的画面。

senses.title: Twisted and tangled
senses.definition: twisted together in tangled masses, said of roots, thread, or hair
senses.definitionCN: 纠结缠绕在一起的，用于形容根、线或头发
senses.example: Her comb got stuck in the knotty hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她的梳子卡在打结的头发里。
senses.why: When many threads are tangled, the tangles take the name of knots, and the adjective spreads to anything that snarls.
senses.whyCN: 许多线缠在一起时，缠团就沿用了「结」的名称，形容词于是也用到一切缠绕之物上。

senses.title: Hard to describe clearly
senses.definition: complicated and dense, said of texts, logic, or arguments that never seem clear
senses.definitionCN: 复杂而密集的，用于形容总是看不清的文本、逻辑或论证
senses.example: The essay was knotty and full of unexplained terms.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章晦涩难懂，满是没解释的术语。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from a problem to the reasoning that has to untie it, so dense writing also reads as knotty.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从问题本身延伸到需要解开的推理过程，所以密集难读的文字也显得 knotty。

intro.en: Knotty is the adjective of knot, an Old English word for a tied fastening or a hard lump in wood, from Germanic.
intro.cn: knotty 是 knot 的形容词，knot 为古英语词，指系成的结或木头上的硬节，源于日耳曼语。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic noun named a knot or a tied bundle; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个重构的日耳曼语名词表示结或捆扎的束，确切形式存疑。

items.en: Cnotta names a knot in rope, thread, or cloth.
items.cn: cnotta 指绳索、线或布料上打的结。

items.en: Knot also names the hard round lump in timber and the joint of a stem.
items.cn: knot 同时指木材中的硬节与茎干上的节。

items.en: Knotty appears as a simple adjective meaning full of knots.
items.cn: knotty 作为简单形容词出现，意为布满结的。

items.en: Knotty begins to describe tangled and puzzling matters of thought and speech.
items.cn: knotty 开始用于描述思想与言语中纠缠难解之事。

items.en: Knotty problem is now the most frequent collocation, with the wood sense kept in fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语中 knotty problem 成为最常见的搭配，木节义则保留在固定说法里。

note.en: Knotty grows from knot with the suffix -y, and its meaning neighbours are the adjectives of difficulty and tanglement.
note.cn: knotty 由 knot 加后缀 -y 构成，意义邻词是表示困难与缠结的形容词。

entries.definition: a fastening made by tying, or a hard lump in wood
entries.definitionCN: 结；木节（knotty 的基础名词）

entries.definition: the quality of being knotty or difficult
entries.definitionCN: 棘手；盘根错节

entries.definition: having no knots
entries.definitionCN: 无结的；无木节的

entries.definition: difficult, like a question full of sharp points
entries.definitionCN: 棘手的（像长满刺一样扎手）

entries.definition: difficult and needing care or skill
entries.definitionCN: 难对付的；需要小心的

entries.definition: twisted together in a messy mass
entries.definitionCN: 缠结的；混乱的

normalIntro.en: Knotty is knot plus -y, so it means full of knots, and what is full of knots is hard to untie.
normalIntro.cn: knotty 是 knot 加 -y，意为「满是结的」，而满是结的东西很难解开。

normal.en: A knotty problem is a problem that will not come apart.
normal.cn: a knotty problem 就是解不开的问题。

normal.en: Knotty pine has many dark hard knots in the wood.
normal.cn: knotty pine 的木料上有许多深色硬节。

normal.en: The suffix -y marks fullness, as in knotty or hairy.
normal.cn: 后缀 -y 表示「充满」，如 knotty 与 hairy。

normal.en: Knottiness is the noun for the quality of being tangled and hard.
normal.cn: knottiness 是名词，表示纠结难办的性质。

normal.en: Compare thorny: thorny stresses sharp risk, knotty stresses tangled complexity.
normal.cn: 对比 thorny：thorny 强调尖锐的风险，knotty 强调纠缠的复杂。

abstract.en: Picture fingers pulling a knot in wet string and only making it tighter.
abstract.cn: 想象手指拉扯湿绳上的结，结果越拉越紧。

abstract.en: Imagine a dark hard knot in a wooden plank that stops the saw.
abstract.cn: 想象木板里一个深色硬节把锯子卡住。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of people all talking at once, each sentence tying to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈人同时说话，每句话都和下一句缠在一起。

examples.en: How to share the water is a knotty question for the villages.
examples.cn: 如何分水对这几个村子来说是个棘手的问题。

examples.en: Knotty wood is hard to sand until it is smooth.
examples.cn: 多节的木料很难打磨光滑。

examples.en: After the storm the hedge was knotty and overgrown.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过后，树篱盘根错节、长得杂乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挠体」——身上缠满结，挠也挠不开，就是棘手的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 cnotta（结）→ knot（结；木节）+ 形容词后缀 -y（充满……的）→ knotty，核心义「布满结、难以解开」。

sensesIntro.en: Knotty begins with wood full of knots, then lends its tanglement to threads, to problems, and to dense writing.
sensesIntro.cn: knotty 先指布满木节的木头，再把「纠结」的形象借给线团、问题与艰深的文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope twisted into tight knots that the fingers cannot loosen.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳子拧成死结，手指怎么也松不开。

branches.en: The main modern sense is the problem that will not come apart.
branches.cn: 现代最主要的义项就是解不开的问题。

branches.en: The literal wood sense keeps the suffix meaning of full of.
branches.cn: 木节义保留了后缀「充满」的字面含义。

branches.en: Tangled roots and hair show the same knots on a soft surface.
branches.cn: 缠结的根与头发展示柔软表面上的同类结。

branches.en: Dense argument is the knot moved into thought and language.
branches.cn: 密集的论证是把结搬进了思想与语言。

branches.en: Hard knots in wood and tangled hair are both physical versions of the core image.
branches.cn: 木头的硬节与打结的头发都是核心意象的物理版本。

intro.en: Knotty is knot plus the suffix -y, and the family grows with knottiness, knotless, and the verb knot.
intro.cn: knotty 由 knot 加后缀 -y 构成，词族包括 knottiness、knotless 以及动词 knot。

latinIntro.en: Knot is a native Germanic word, so the Latin forms here are only comparing shapes for knots and tangles, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: knot 是本土日耳曼词，这里的拉丁形式只是表示「结、缠绕」的可比形状，并非来源。

items.meaning: a tied fastening or a hard lump
items.example: Knot is the base of the adjective knotty.
items.exampleCN: knot 是形容词 knotty 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 充满……的；具有……特征的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y makes knot into knotty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 knot 变成 knotty。

items.example: Knotty carries both the wood sense and the problem sense.
items.exampleCN: knotty 兼具木节义与问题义。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms knottiness.

items.meaning: the state of being tangled or difficult

items.exampleCN: knottiness 指困难本身。

items.example: The suffix -less forms knotless.

items.example: Knotless thread does not snag.
items.exampleCN: 无结的线不会勾住。

items.example: To knot a rope is to tie it firmly.
items.exampleCN: knot a rope 就是把绳子牢牢打结。

items.example: The compound keeps the wood sense visible.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词让木节义也看得见。

latinEntries.example: Nodus is a comparing form and not the source of knot.
