latinEntries.example: Implicare gives a useful picture of tangling.
latinEntries.exampleCN: implicare 提供了「缠绕」的画面供对照。

definition_zh: 考拉；树袋熊；考拉毛皮
definition_en: a small grey Australian marsupial that lives in eucalyptus trees and feeds on their leaves
core_image: 一只灰色毛茸茸的小兽抱紧桉树，叼着叶子慢慢嚼
scene: 动物园里一只考拉抱着树干打盹，饲养员在旁边轻声走动。At the zoo a sleepy koala hugged the trunk while the keeper walked past quietly.
sceneCN: 这里 koala 指「考拉」（第 1 个义项：澳洲树栖的有袋类动物，主要以桉树叶为食）；句意：动物园里，一只困倦的考拉抱着树干，饲养员从旁边轻声走过。

pos.zh: 考拉；树袋熊；考拉毛皮

derivatives.zh: koala 的旧拼写形式，源于殖民时期对达鲁格语的记音，如今已罕用
由 koala 与 bear 组合的通俗说法，指考拉，但考拉并非熊类
考拉的拉丁学属名，由分类学家另造，与 koala 词源无关，仅供对照

senses.title: The tree-living marsupial
senses.definition: a small grey Australian marsupial with a big nose and round ears that lives in eucalyptus trees
senses.definitionCN: 一种生活在澳大利亚、灰色、大鼻子圆耳朵、栖息在桉树上的小型有袋动物
senses.example: A koala sleeps for much of the day in a fork of the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 考拉一天大部分时间都睡在树杈间。
senses.why: The animal is named for the tree it lives in, so the noun first names a creature bonded to the eucalyptus.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物以它栖身的树命名，所以名词首先指向一种与桉树绑定的动物。

senses.title: The species as a whole
senses.definition: the species or population considered together, as in talks of conservation
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的考拉物种或种群，常见于保护话题
senses.example: The koala is now listed as a vulnerable species in some states.
senses.exampleCN: 在一些州，考拉现在被列为易危物种。
senses.why: In nature writing one definite noun often stands for the whole species, so koala can mean all its members.
senses.whyCN: 在自然写作中，一个定指名词常代表整个物种，所以 koala 也可以指全部成员。

senses.title: The fur of the animal
senses.definition: the dense grey fur of a koala, used in old trade descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 考拉厚密的灰色毛皮，多见于旧时的贸易描述
senses.example: The coat was trimmed with koala in the old catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧目录里，这件外套镶着考拉毛皮。
senses.why: Words for fur-bearing animals often name their skins too, an older and now rare use.
senses.whyCN: 皮毛类动物的名称常直接指其毛皮，这是一种较早、如今少见的用法。

senses.title: A toy or soft figure
senses.definition: a toy or decorative figure shaped like a koala
senses.definitionCN: 做考拉形状的玩具或装饰摆件
senses.example: She bought a koala for her little brother at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她在机场给弟弟买了一只考拉玩偶。
senses.why: Popular animals become toys and souvenirs, and the animal name itself names the object.
senses.whyCN: 受欢迎的动物会变成玩具和纪念品，动物名称就直接用来指那个物件。

intro.en: Koala comes from the Dharug language of the Sydney region, where it was first recorded by English settlers.
intro.cn: koala 源自悉尼地区的达鲁格语，最早由英国移民记录。

items.en: Dharug speakers use the word for the animal; the exact meaning is debated, with some sources giving no water.
items.cn: 达鲁格语使用者用它称呼这种动物；其确切含义有争议，有资料称意为「不喝水」。

items.en: Early colonial records first set down the word in English spelling during exploration of the Blue Mountains.
items.cn: 在一七九八年探索蓝山地区的早期殖民记录中，这个词第一次以英语拼写被记下。

items.en: Spellings such as koolah, koola, and coola circulate, and koala settles later.
items.cn: koolah、koola、coola 等拼写一度通行，koala 后来才固定下来。

items.en: Colonial texts call the animal a native bear, and the phrase koala bear follows.
items.cn: 殖民时期的文本把它叫作 native bear，随后出现 koala bear 这一说法。

items.en: Koala is the standard name, and koala bear is kept only as a common, loose tag.
items.cn: 现代英语中 koala 是标准名称，koala bear 只作为常见但不严谨的叫法保留。

note.en: Koala is a borrowed Australian word with no Latin root, and its neighbours are marsupials, eucalyptus trees, and familiar animals.
note.cn: koala 是借用自澳洲原住民语言的词，没有拉丁词根，意义邻词是有袋类、桉树与常见动物。

entries.definition: an early colonial spelling of koala
entries.definitionCN: koala 的早期殖民时期拼写

entries.definition: a large Australian kingfisher with a loud call
entries.definitionCN: 澳洲的大翠鸟（同属澳洲原住民来源的词，词根不同）

entries.definition: a small kangaroo-like marsupial of Australia
entries.definitionCN: 澳洲的小袋鼠类（同为澳洲原住民借词，含义不同）

entries.definition: a stocky Australian marsupial that digs burrows
entries.definitionCN: 澳洲袋熊（同科的地栖有袋类）

entries.definition: a marsupial of the Americas that climbs trees
entries.definitionCN: 美洲的树栖有袋类

entries.definition: the tall gum tree whose leaves koalas eat
entries.definitionCN: 桉树（考拉的食物来源）

normalIntro.en: Koala is a borrowed Dharug word that names the climber of the eucalyptus, not a bear, and not a Latin animal name.
normalIntro.cn: koala 是借用自达鲁格语的词，指吃桉树的攀爬者，既不是熊，也不是拉丁语动物名。

normal.en: Koala bear is a loose popular tag, because a koala is a marsupial, not a bear.
normal.cn: koala bear 只是通俗叫法，因为考拉是有袋类而不是熊。

normal.en: A koala sanctuary protects trees and rescues injured animals.
normal.cn: koala sanctuary 指保护树木、救助受伤考拉的保护区。

normal.en: The koala population fell as forests were cleared for housing.
normal.cn: koala population 随着森林被砍伐建房而减少。

normal.en: The word is spelled koalas in the plural, with a simple -s.
normal.cn: 复数拼作 koalas，只加一个 -s。

normal.en: Compare wombat: wombat digs a burrow, while koala lives in a tree.
normal.cn: 对比 wombat：袋熊挖洞，考拉住在树上。

abstract.en: Picture grey fur wrapped around a white tree trunk, eyes half shut.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色毛团缠在白色树干上，半闭着眼睛。

abstract.en: Imagine the slow chewing of a eucalyptus leaf, one side then the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一片桉树叶被慢慢嚼着，先一侧再另一侧。

abstract.en: Picture a forest of gum trees where every fork holds a sleeping climber.
abstract.cn: 想象一片桉树林，每个树杈上都睡着一个攀爬者。

examples.en: The koala at the sanctuary hardly moved for hours.
examples.cn: 保护区里的那只考拉好几个小时几乎没动。

examples.en: Fires destroyed much of the koala habitat last summer.
examples.cn: 去年夏天的火灾毁掉了考拉的大片栖息地。

examples.en: A pair of koalas shared the same tree at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时两只考拉共用同一棵树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扣啦」——考拉抱着树，爪子扣得紧紧的，扣住就不下来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 达鲁格语（澳洲新南威尔士悉尼一带的原住民语言）gula / koolah（一七九八年进入英语拼写）→ 英语 koala；它并非拉丁或希腊构词，也无可靠的反向构词来源。

sensesIntro.en: Koala first names one tree-dwelling animal, then its whole species, its fur, and finally toys shaped like it.
sensesIntro.cn: koala 先指一种住在树上的动物，再指整个物种、它的毛皮，最后指仿其形状的玩具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey climber locked onto a gum tree, chewing leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只灰色小兽紧抱桉树，慢慢嚼着叶子。

branches.en: The single animal is the everyday sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 指单个动物是名词最日常的义项。

branches.en: The species sense appears in conservation talk.
branches.cn: 物种义项出现在保护话题中。

branches.en: The fur sense belongs to older trade language.
branches.cn: 毛皮义项属于较旧的贸易语言。

branches.en: A toy bear takes the animal name directly.
branches.cn: 考拉玩偶直接沿用了动物名称。

branches.en: One animal, its species, and its toy all share the same familiar image.
branches.cn: 一只考拉、整个物种和考拉玩偶都共享同一个熟悉形象。

intro.en: Koala is a loanword, so it takes no productive English affixes beyond the plural -s and compounds such as koala bear.
intro.cn: koala 是外来词，除复数 -s 与 koala bear 这类合成词外，没有可产出的英语词缀参与构词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for koala, so the shared-root list stays empty, and only the taxonomists genus name is noted in the items.
latinIntro.cn: koala 没有拉丁语来源，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空，只在构词条目里说明分类学家另造的属名。

items.example: Koala is the standard modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: koala 是现代标准拼写。

items.example: The plural koalas simply adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数 koalas 只是加 -s。

items.meaning: a common but loose name for the koala
items.meaningCN: 考拉的通俗不严谨叫法
items.example: Koala bear mixes a marsupial name with a bear name.
items.exampleCN: koala bear 把有袋类名称与熊的名称混在一起。

items.example: To protect koala habitat is to protect gum trees.
items.exampleCN: 保护考拉栖息地就是保护桉树林。

items.meaning: the number of koalas in an area
items.example: The koala population is falling in some regions.
items.exampleCN: 在一些地区，考拉数量正在下降。

items.example: A koala sanctuary looks after injured animals.
items.exampleCN: 考拉保护区照料受伤的动物。

items.meaning: the genus name of the koala
items.example: Phascolarctos cinereus is the scientific name, built from Greek parts by taxonomists, not from the Dharug word.
items.exampleCN: 学名 Phascolarctos cinereus 由分类学家用希腊语词根拼成，并非来自达鲁格语。

items.meaning: a mammal that carries its young in a pouch
items.example: Koala is a marsupial, so its baby lives in a pouch.
items.exampleCN: 考拉是有袋类，所以幼崽住在育儿袋里。

items.meaning: the gum tree koalas live in
items.example: Koalas eat mainly eucalyptus leaves.
items.exampleCN: 这动物的主要食物就是桉树叶。

definition_zh: 费力的；艰难的；艰苦的
definition_en: needing a lot of effort and time; slow and heavy to do
core_image: 一个人弯着腰，吃力地推着满载的石碾
scene: 全班花了一整个学期整理旧档案。Sorting all those old files felt laborious for everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 laborious 是「费力的、耗时的」（第 1 个义项：需要大量努力和时间）；句意：整理那些旧档案让每个人都觉得很费力。

pos.zh: 费力的；艰难的；艰苦的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「费力地；艰难地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「费力；艰苦」
荷兰语与古法语形式，名词义为「劳动；劳务」；美式拼作 labor
labor 加 -er 构成，义为「劳工；体力劳动者」

senses.title: Needing much effort and time
senses.definition: requiring a great deal of effort, patience, and time to complete
senses.definitionCN: 完成起来需要大量精力、耐心和时间
senses.example: Copying every page by hand was a laborious job.
senses.exampleCN: 亲手抄写每一页是一项费力的工作。
senses.why: The Latin root labor means toil and physical work, so anything laborious carries the weight of heavy labour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 labor 意为劳作与苦干，所以 laborious 天生带着沉重劳作的重量感。

senses.title: Full of hard work
senses.definition: marked by long hours of tiring, physical or mental work
senses.definitionCN: 以长时间的、令人疲惫的体力或脑力工作为特征
senses.example: Farmers face a laborious life during the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在收获季节过着艰苦繁忙的生活。
senses.why: The word can describe a whole way of life that is filled with exhausting work rather than one single task.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅可以形容一项任务，还能形容一种被繁重劳动填满的生活方式。

senses.title: Shown through effort
senses.definition: done with visible effort and diligent, steady application
senses.definitionCN: 带着明显的努力、以勤奋踏实的方式完成
senses.example: Her laborious reading of the poem showed real care.
senses.exampleCN: 她逐字逐句费力地读那首诗，显出真正的用心。
senses.why: Effort itself becomes something visible, so the adjective can praise a careful and thorough manner.
senses.whyCN: 努力本身成了看得见的东西，于是这个词也能用来称赞细致扎实的做事方式。

senses.title: Slow and heavy in style
senses.definition: used of writing or speech that is slow, heavy, and hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 形容文字或讲话缓慢沉重、难以理解
senses.example: The report was long and laborious to get through.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告又长又难读，读起来很吃力。
senses.why: Reading is also work, so a heavy style that demands effort is called laborious.
senses.whyCN: 阅读同样是一种劳动，所以需要读者费力才能读下去的风格也被称为 laborious。

intro.en: Laborious comes from Latin laboriosus, full of toil, built on labor, meaning work or hardship.
intro.cn: laborious 来自拉丁语 laboriosus（充满辛劳的），由 labor（劳动、艰辛）构成。

items.en: Labor means work, toil, or hardship.
items.cn: labor 意为劳动、辛苦、艰难。

items.en: Laboriosus describes something full of toil.
items.cn: laboriosus 形容充满辛劳的东西。

items.en: Laborieux carries the adjective into French.
items.cn: laborieux 把这个形容词带入法语。

items.en: Laborious appears in English meaning full of labour.
items.cn: laborious 进入英语，最初意为「充满劳作的」。

items.en: The meaning widens to any task or style that takes much effort.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到任何需要大量努力的任务或文体。

note.en: Laborious belongs to the Latin labor family, and sits next to ordinary effort words such as hard, tiring, and strenuous.
note.cn: laborious 属于拉丁语 labor 词族，与 hard、tiring、strenuous 等表示「费力」的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: with great effort and in a slow, careful way
entries.definitionCN: 费力地；缓慢而仔细地

entries.definition: the quality of needing much effort
entries.definitionCN: 费力；艰苦

entries.definition: work, especially hard physical work
entries.definitionCN: 劳动；尤指繁重的体力劳动

entries.definition: needing great effort and usually energy or strength
entries.definitionCN: 艰巨的；费力的

entries.definition: using a lot of energy or effort
entries.definitionCN: 费力的；需要全力的

entries.definition: too long, slow, and boring
entries.definitionCN: 冗长乏味的

normalIntro.en: Laborious carries Latin labor inside it, so the word always smells of sweat and hard work.
normalIntro.cn: laborious 里装着拉丁语的 labor，所以这个词总带着汗水和苦干的味道。

normal.en: Labor plus -ious means full of labour, hence needing much effort.
normal.cn: labor 加后缀 -ious 表示「充满劳作」，因此就是「费力的」。

normal.en: The adverb laboriously keeps the same meaning.
normal.cn: 副词 laboriously 保持了同样的含义。

normal.en: A laborious task takes patience as much as strength.
normal.cn: laborious task 这种任务既耗力气也耗耐心。

normal.en: Compare labor, labourer, and labor move, all built on the same root.
normal.cn: 对比 labor、labourer 与 labor move，这些都建立在同一个词根上。

normal.en: Another word from the same family is elaborate, which means worked out with much care.
normal.cn: 同一词族的另一个词是「elaborate」，意为精心制作出来的。

abstract.en: Picture a mountain of paper on a desk late at night.
abstract.cn: 想象深夜里桌上一摞像山一样的文件。

abstract.en: Feel the sweat on a back bent over a field all day.
abstract.cn: 感受整天弯着腰在田间劳作时背上渗出的汗。

abstract.en: Hear a pen scratching slowly line after line, never speeding up.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖一行接一行地慢慢划动，始终快不起来。

examples.en: Checking every single number by hand is a laborious process.
examples.cn: 手工核对每一个数字是一个繁琐的过程。

examples.en: They made a laborious climb up the icy slope.
examples.cn: 他们在结冰的坡上艰难地爬行。

examples.en: Translating the old manuscript was slow and laborious work.
examples.cn: 翻译那份旧手稿是既慢又费力的工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「勒伯瑞」——勒紧、伯父喘、瑞气喘，推着石碾走一圈都费劲；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 labor（劳动；辛苦）→ laboriosus（充满辛劳的）→ 古法语 laborieux → 英语 laborious，核心义「带着沉重劳作」。

sensesIntro.en: Laborious starts from the weight of hard work and spreads to a way of life, a visible effort, and finally a heavy style of writing.
sensesIntro.cn: laborious 从「沉重劳作」这一重量感出发，扩展到一种生活方式、看得见的努力，最后指沉重的文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bent back pushing a heavy stone roller.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个弯着腰推沉重石碾的人。

branches.en: A task that demands great effort is the core sense.
branches.cn: 需要大量努力的任务是核心义项。

branches.en: A life full of toil is the general sense.
branches.cn: 充满劳作的生活是概括性义项。

branches.en: Effort made visible becomes a matter of manner.
branches.cn: 努力的可见化落到做事方式上。

branches.en: Heavy prose turns reading into labour.
branches.cn: 沉重的文字让阅读本身变成一种劳作。

branches.en: Single tasks and whole lives can both be described as full of work.
branches.cn: 单项任务与整个人生都可以被称为充满劳作。

intro.en: Laborious is built from Latin labor plus the adjective ending -ious, with -ly and -ness extending the family.
intro.cn: laborious 由拉丁语 labor 加形容词词尾 -ious 构成，再借 -ly 与 -ness 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor means work or hardship, and laboriosus means full of toil.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 labor 意为劳动或艰辛，laboriosus 意为充满辛劳的。

items.example: Laborare supplies the working root.
items.exampleCN: laborare 提供「劳作」这一词根。

items.example: Labor is the direct base of the word.
items.exampleCN: labor 是这个形容词的直接词基。

items.meaning: full of, having the nature of
items.meaningCN: 充满……的；具有……性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ious turns labor into laborious.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ious 把 labor 变成 laborious。

items.example: Laborious keeps the full-of-toil sense.
items.exampleCN: laborious 保留了「充满辛劳」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms laboriously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 laboriously。

items.example: Laboriously describes the way of doing something.
items.exampleCN: laboriously 描述做事的方式。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms laboriousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 laboriousness。

items.example: Laboriousness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: laboriousness 指这种性质本身。

items.example: The suffix -er forms laborer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 laborer。

items.meaning: a person who does hard work
items.example: Laborer is the person noun of labor.
items.exampleCN: laborer 是 labor 的人物名词。

definition_zh: 瓢虫；瓢虫科甲虫
definition_en: a small round red or yellow beetle with black spots that eats plant pests
core_image: 一片绿叶上停着一只红底黑点的圆甲虫
scene: 菜园的小叶子上停着一只红底黑点的圆虫。A small ladybug rested on a leaf of the vegetable garden.
sceneCN: 这里 ladybug 是「瓢虫」（第 1 个义项：红或黄色带黑点的圆形甲虫）；句意：菜园的一片叶子上停着一只小瓢虫。

pos.zh: 瓢虫；瓢虫科甲虫

derivatives.zh: 英式说法，由 lady 与 bird 组合，义为「瓢虫」，与美式 ladybug 同义
组合词的前半部分，本义为「女士；淑女」，与 bug（小虫）合成瓢虫之名
组合词的后半部分，义为「小虫子；昆虫」
正式说法，由 lady 与 beetle（甲虫）组合，义为「瓢虫」

senses.title: The familiar spotted beetle
senses.definition: a small dome-shaped beetle, usually red or yellow with black spots
senses.definitionCN: 一种小型圆顶甲虫，通常为红或黄色并带黑点
senses.example: A ladybug crawled along the stem.
senses.exampleCN: 一只瓢虫沿着茎爬行。
senses.why: The name joins lady and bug, a small beetle once named after the Virgin Mary in honour of its red coat.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字由 lady 与 bug 组成，因为其红色外衣，人们曾借圣母之名来称呼这种小甲虫。

senses.title: A natural pest eater
senses.definition: the insect seen as a helpful garden creature that feeds on aphids
senses.definitionCN: 被视为有益的花园生物，以蚜虫为食
senses.example: Farmers welcome ladybugs because they eat tiny plant pests.
senses.exampleCN: 农民欢迎瓢虫，因为它们会吃掉植物上的小害虫。
senses.why: In gardens the creature is valued for its appetite, so the name also stands for a useful ally.
senses.whyCN: 在花园里，这种生物因其食量而受重视，于是名字也代表一位有用的帮手。

senses.title: Spotted pattern and shape
senses.titleCN: 瓢虫斑纹；瓢虫般的圆点图案
senses.definition: the red-and-black dotted look borrowed from the insect
senses.definitionCN: 借用这种昆虫而来的红底黑点外观
senses.example: Her rain boots were covered in little ladybugs.
senses.exampleCN: 她的雨靴上印满了小瓢虫图案。
senses.why: The vivid rounded look is easy to copy, so the word names a decorative pattern too.
senses.whyCN: 这种醒目的圆润外观很容易被模仿，于是这个词也用来指一种装饰图案。

senses.title: A name for something small and round
senses.definition: used playfully for a small round child or object
senses.definitionCN: 戏称小巧圆圆的孩童或物品
senses.example: The toddler was bundled up like a tiny ladybug.
senses.exampleCN: 那个蹒跚学步的孩子被裹得像一只小瓢虫。
senses.why: The insect is tiny, round, and bright, so it becomes an affectionate nickname for small round things.
senses.whyCN: 这种虫子小巧、圆润又鲜艳，于是成了称呼小巧圆润事物的亲昵比喻。

intro.en: Ladybug is an English compound of lady and bug, and it echoes older names that linked the red beetle with the Virgin Mary.
intro.cn: ladybug 是英语中 lady 与 bug 的复合词，呼应了早期把红色甲虫与圣母联系起来的称呼。

items.en: The scientific family name Coccinellidae comes from coccineus, meaning scarlet.
items.cn: 科学上的科名 Coccinellidae 来自拉丁语 coccineus，意为深红。

items.en: European names such as ladybird and German Marienkaefer connect the insect with the Virgin Mary.
items.cn: 欧洲的称谓如 ladybird 与德语 Marienkaefer 都把这种昆虫与圣母联系在一起。

items.en: The compound ladybird is recorded in Britain, with bird used loosely for any small flying creature.
items.cn: ladybird 这一复合词在英国的记录可追至十七世纪，其中 bird 泛称会飞的小生物。

items.en: American speakers replace bird with bug, giving ladybug.
items.cn: 美国使用者用 bug 取代 bird，形成了 ladybug。

items.en: Entomologists also use the neutral term lady beetle.
items.cn: 昆虫学家也使用中性的说法「lady beetle」。

note.en: Ladybug is a simple compound name for a spotted beetle, close in form to ladybird and lady beetle, and close in meaning to beetle and other garden insects.
note.cn: ladybug 是表示带斑甲虫的简单复合名称，形近词有 ladybird 与 lady beetle，近义词有 beetle 等花园昆虫。

entries.definition: the British name for the same spotted beetle
entries.definitionCN: 同一类带斑甲虫的英式称呼

entries.definition: the careful or scientific name of the same insect
entries.definitionCN: 同一昆虫的严谨或科学称呼

entries.definition: a small insect, the second half of the name
entries.definitionCN: 小虫子，是这个词的后半部分

entries.definition: an insect with hard, shiny wing cases
entries.definitionCN: 甲虫；有坚硬亮翅鞘的昆虫

entries.definition: a very small insect that sucks plant juices
entries.definitionCN: 蚜虫；吸食植物汁液的小虫

entries.definition: a small beetle that glows in the dark
entries.definitionCN: 萤火虫

normalIntro.en: Ladybug is easy to remember: put lady and bug together and picture a team of tiny spotted beetles.
normalIntro.cn: ladybug 很好记：把 lady 与 bug 拼在一起，想象一队带斑点的小甲虫。

normal.en: LADY plus BUG, so think of a lady in a red polka-dot coat.
normal.cn: LADY 加 BUG，就想象一位穿着红色圆点外衣的女士。

normal.en: British speakers say ladybird, American speakers say ladybug.
normal.cn: 英国人说 ladybird，美国人说 ladybug。

normal.en: The plural is simply ladybugs.
normal.cn: 复数只要在词尾加 s，写成 ladybugs。

normal.en: A ladybug is a beetle, not a true bug in the scientific sense.
normal.cn: 瓢虫属于甲虫，在科学分类上并不是严格的 bug 类。

normal.en: As a garden helper it eats aphids, so growers protect it.
normal.cn: 它作为花园帮手会吃蚜虫，所以种植者会保护它。

abstract.en: Imagine a red dome with black spots crawling up a green stem.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带黑点的红色圆顶顺着绿色茎向上爬。

abstract.en: See hundreds of them landing on a rose bush to hunt tiny pests.
abstract.cn: 想象成百上千只落在玫瑰丛上捕捉小害虫。

abstract.en: Picture a child in a red dotted raincoat, round and bright as a bug.
abstract.cn: 想象一个穿红色圆点雨衣的孩子，圆圆亮亮的像只小虫。

examples.en: A ladybug landed on the picnic blanket and opened its wings.
examples.cn: 一只瓢虫落在野餐毯上，展开了翅膀。

examples.en: Gardeners often introduce ladybugs to protect their roses.
examples.cn: 园丁常引入瓢虫来保护他们的玫瑰。

examples.en: In autumn ladybugs gather together before the cold weather arrives.
examples.cn: 秋季天冷之前，瓢虫会聚集成群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累滴宝」——小巧的宝，滴溜溜在叶子上爬；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 lady（女士；由圣母之名引申）+ bug（小虫），与英式 ladybird、德语 Marienkaefer 一样，都源自把红色甲虫与圣母相联的民间称呼；不是拉丁语源词。

sensesIntro.en: Ladybug names the spotted beetle itself, then the valued pest eater, then a dotted pattern, and finally any small round thing used affectionately.
sensesIntro.cn: ladybug 先指带斑点的瓢虫本身，再指受重视的灭虫益虫，然后是圆点图案，最后戏称任何小巧圆润的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red-and-black dome resting on a green leaf.
core.cn: 核心意象：停在一片绿叶上的红黑圆顶小甲虫。

branches.en: The beetle itself is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 这种甲虫本身是基础义项。

branches.en: Its appetite makes it a welcome garden helper.
branches.cn: 它的食性让它成为受欢迎的花园帮手。

branches.en: Its colouring is borrowed as a pattern.
branches.cn: 它的配色被借用为图案。

branches.en: Its small round shape becomes a playful name.
branches.cn: 它小巧圆润的外形成了俏皮的称呼。

branches.en: The insect and its pattern share the same red-and-black dots.
branches.cn: 昆虫本身与它的图案共享同样的红底黑点。

intro.en: Ladybug is a native English compound of lady and bug, not a Latin or Greek formation, so the word-family notes below are mostly about compounding.
intro.cn: ladybug 是英语本土的复合词，由 lady 与 bug 组成，并非拉丁或希腊构词，因此下面讲的构词条目主要关于复合。

latinIntro.en: The modern scientific name is from Latin, where Coccinellidae comes from coccineus, scarlet; but the folk names ladybird and ladybug are English compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 现代科学名称来自拉丁语，如 Coccinellidae 源于 coccineus（深红）；但民间称呼 ladybird 与 ladybug 都是英语复合词。

items.meaning: a woman, or the Virgin Mary in old use
items.example: Lady is the first part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: lady 是这个复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Bug is the second part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: bug 是这个复合词的后半部分。

items.example: Ladybug is the American compound name.
items.exampleCN: ladybug 是美式复合名称。

items.meaning: the British name for the insect
items.example: Ladybird uses bird instead of bug.
items.exampleCN: ladybird 用 bird 取代了 bug。

items.meaning: the careful name for the insect
items.example: Lady beetle avoids the word bug.
items.exampleCN: lady beetle 避开了 bug 这个词。

items.example: Coccinellidae is the scientific family name.
items.exampleCN: Coccinellidae 是科学上的科名。

items.example: Coccineus explains the red coat in the scientific name.
items.exampleCN: coccineus 解释了科学名称里的红色外衣。

items.meaning: family, used to form family names
items.example: The suffix -idae forms family names such as Coccinellidae.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -idae 构成 Coccinellidae 这样的科名。

items.example: Ladybugs takes a simple plural -s.
items.exampleCN: ladybugs 只加一个复数 -s。

definition_zh: 跛的；瘸的；站不住脚的；蹩脚的
definition_en: unable to walk well because of an injured or weak leg, or weak and unconvincing
core_image: 一个人扶着墙，一只脚拖在地上勉强行走
scene: 他上周摔伤了腿，走路时一瘸一拐。Since the fall, my uncle has been lame for weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 lame 是「跛的、瘸的」（第 1 个义项：因腿伤或腿弱而走不好路）；句意：摔伤以来，我叔叔已经瘸了好几周。

pos.zh: 跛的；瘸的
站不住脚的；蹩脚的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「无力地；拙劣地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「跛；无力」
lame 与 brain 组合的口语词，义为「笨蛋」
来自法语的织物名，义为「金银线织物」，只是拼写相近，词源不同

senses.title: Unable to walk properly
senses.definition: unable to walk well because of an injury, disease, or weakness in the leg or foot
senses.definitionCN: 因腿脚受伤、患病或无力而无法正常行走
senses.example: The old dog was lame in one hind leg.
senses.exampleCN: 那条老狗的一条后腿瘸了。
senses.why: The oldest sense describes a body that cannot move smoothly, standing for a broken stride.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义描述的是无法顺畅移动的身体，代表着被打断的步伐。

senses.title: Weak and unconvincing
senses.definition: used of an excuse, argument, or reason that is weak and easily seen through
senses.definitionCN: 形容借口、论点或理由薄弱，容易被人看穿
senses.example: He gave a lame excuse for missing the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他为错过截止时间找了一个站不住脚的借口。
senses.why: An excuse that cannot stand up has the same failing leg: it cannot bear the weight of scrutiny.
senses.whyCN: 站不住的借口就像瘸了的腿，承受不起别人推敲的重量。

senses.title: Poor or unconvincing in quality
senses.definition: describing something dull, weak, or badly made, such as a joke or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 形容笑话、表演等乏味、无力或做得粗糙
senses.example: The film ended with a lame punchline.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影以一个蹩脚的包袱收尾。
senses.why: From weak arguments the word spreads to anything that fails to deliver, so a flat joke is lame too.
senses.whyCN: 从无力的论点扩展到一切达不到效果的东西，所以冷掉的笑话也叫 lame。

senses.title: Old-fashioned and slightly rude
senses.definition: used in old slang for something dull, uncool, or a killjoy person
senses.definitionCN: 旧时俚语中指乏味、不时髦的人或事
senses.example: Some teenagers still say a party was lame.
senses.exampleCN: 一些青少年仍会说某个聚会很没劲。
senses.why: Slang borrows the image of a broken walk to mock anything that limps along without energy.
senses.whyCN: 俚语借用「跛行」的画面，来嘲讽一切缺少活力、走不顺畅的事物。

intro.en: Lame is an old Germanic word, recorded in English from before the twelfth century, and it is related to similar words in other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: lame 是一个古老的日耳曼词，英语记录可追溯到十二世纪以前，与其他日耳曼语言中的同源词相关。

items.en: A reconstructed root with the sense of bending or being bent is usually connected with the word.
items.cn: 一般认为它与一个表示「弯曲」的重构词根有关。

items.en: The reconstructed form means weak in the limbs, especially in the legs.
items.cn: 其重构形式意为四肢、尤指腿脚虚弱。

items.en: Lama is recorded in Old English for a person or animal unable to walk well.
items.cn: 古英语 lama 指行走不便的人或动物。

items.en: Lame keeps the physical sense and grows in use.
items.cn: 中古英语 lame 保留了身体含义，使用范围扩大。

items.en: The word extends figuratively to weak excuses and dull jokes.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到薄弱的借口和乏味的笑话。

note.en: Lame is a short Germanic adjective, close in spelling to the French fabric word lame, and close in meaning to crippled, halting, and weak.
note.cn: lame 是简短的日耳曼形容词，拼写与法语织物词 lame 相近，意思上与 crippled、halting、weak 等词相邻。

entries.definition: in a weak or unconvincing way
entries.definitionCN: 无力地；拙劣地

entries.definition: the state of being lame
entries.definitionCN: 跛；无力

entries.definition: a silly person, in informal use
entries.definitionCN: 笨蛋；傻瓜（口语）

entries.definition: seriously disabled, now avoided in careful speech
entries.definitionCN: 有严重残疾的；如今应避免使用

entries.definition: stopping and starting, as in slow speech or steps
entries.definitionCN: 间歇的；结结巴巴的

entries.definition: lacking strength or force
entries.definitionCN: 薄弱的；无力的

normalIntro.en: Lame is a small old word: a broken walk comes first, and weak excuses follow from it.
normalIntro.cn: lame 是一个简短古老的词：先是一条走不顺的腿，接着是站不住的借口。

normal.en: Lame keeps the same form whether it describes a dog or an excuse.
normal.cn: lame 无论是形容狗还是形容借口，形式都不变。

normal.en: The comparative is lamer and the superlative is lamest.
normal.cn: 比较级是 lamer，最高级是 lamest。

normal.en: Lame excuse is the most common figurative collocation.
normal.cn: lame excuse（蹩脚的借口）是最常见的比喻搭配。

normal.en: Lamely and lameness are the direct word-family members.
normal.cn: lamely 与 lameness 是最直接的词族成员。

normal.en: Do not confuse lame with lame, the French fabric word with an acute accent.
normal.cn: 不要把它和表示「金银线织物」的法语词 lame 弄混，后者带重音符号。

abstract.en: Hear one foot dragging on the floor, slower than the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚在地板上拖着走，比另一只慢。

abstract.en: See a broken chair leg that cannot carry any weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一条断了的椅腿，承受不住任何重量。

abstract.en: Picture a joke told too slowly, and the room stays silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一个讲得太慢的笑话，满屋沉默。

examples.en: After the accident he walked with a lame left leg for months.
examples.cn: 出事故后，他好几个月左腿都是瘸的。

examples.en: Saying the bus was late is a lame excuse when you left an hour early.
examples.cn: 你提前一小时出门还说公交晚点，是个站不住脚的借口。

examples.en: The team was booed for its lame performance.
examples.cn: 这支队伍因表现差劲而被喝倒彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累」——腿累了就走不动，一步一瘸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 源自古英语 lama（跛的），属日耳曼语系同源词，一般认为与表示「弯曲」的印欧词根相关（重构形式）；与拉丁语和古法语无直接承继关系。

sensesIntro.en: Lame begins with a leg that cannot carry the body, extends to an argument that cannot carry scrutiny, and then to anything weak or dull.
sensesIntro.cn: lame 始于一条撑不起身体的腿，扩展到经不起推敲的论点，再泛指一切薄弱乏味之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body leaning on a wall, one foot dragging.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个扶着墙、一只脚拖地行走的人。

branches.en: The walking body is the physical core.
branches.cn: 行走的身体是身体层面的核心。

branches.en: A reason that cannot stand is a lame excuse.
branches.cn: 站不住的理由就是 lame excuse。

branches.en: Weakness of quality grows out of weakness of step.
branches.cn: 品质上的无力从步伐的无力生长出来。

branches.en: Old slang turns the word into a mild insult.
branches.cn: 旧时俚语把词义变成轻度贬称。

branches.en: Both a leg and an excuse can fail to carry weight.
branches.cn: 腿和借口都可能撑不住重量。

intro.en: Lame is a single Germanic root word, so its family is built with English endings such as -ly, -ness, and compounds like lamebrain.
intro.cn: lame 是单一日耳曼词根词，其词族依靠英语词尾 -ly、-ness 以及 lamebrain 这样的复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Lame has no Latin ancestor; it descends from Germanic forms, so the Latin-source notes below are limited to loan words that merely look similar.
latinIntro.cn: lame 没有拉丁语祖先，而是源自日耳曼语形式；因此下面关于拉丁来源的说明只涉及外观相似的外来词。

items.example: Lama is the Old English ancestor.
items.exampleCN: lama 是古英语的前身形式。

items.example: Lame keeps the old form with a changed vowel.
items.exampleCN: lame 保留了旧形式，只是元音发生变化。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms lamely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 lamely。

items.example: Lamely is used for weak speech and argument.
items.exampleCN: lamely 用于形容无力的言辞和论证。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms lameness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 lameness。

items.example: Lameness names the state itself.
items.exampleCN: lameness 指这种状态本身。

items.example: Brain is the second part of lamebrain.
items.exampleCN: brain 是 lamebrain 的后半部分。

items.example: Lamebrain combines lame with brain.
items.exampleCN: lamebrain 由 lame 与 brain 组合而成。

items.meaning: an official with little power left
items.example: Lame duck is an idiom built from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: lame duck 是由这个形容词构成的习语。

definition_zh: 着陆器；登陆器；移民；船靠岸时的动作
definition_en: a spacecraft or vehicle designed to set down safely on a planet, moon, or other body, or a person who comes to live in a place
core_image: 一台带着支架的小小探测器，缓缓压住陌生的地面，扬起一圈尘土
scene: 工程师们盯着屏幕，探测器在火星表面放下支架，稳妥地站住。After a long fall through thin air, the lander settled safely on the red dust.
sceneCN: 这里 lander 是「着陆器」（第 1 个义项：能够安全降落在星球或卫星表面的航天器）；句意为穿过稀薄大气长途下坠后，着陆器稳稳落在红色尘土上。

pos.zh: 着陆器；登陆器（可数，复数 landers）

derivatives.zh: 基础动词「落地、着陆」也是全词的字面来源：lander 就是「落地的那一位」
land 加 -ing 构成动名词：降落、着陆；也指楼梯平台的歇脚处
形近勿混：hard-liner 指立场强硬的坚持者，其中的 liner 与 land 无关
形近勿混：gander 指雄雁，也可口语指「瞄一眼」，与 land 没有词源关系

senses.title: A craft that sets down on a surface
senses.titleCN: 着陆器：能安全降落在星球表面的航天器
senses.definition: a spacecraft built to descend and set down intact on the surface of a moon, planet, or similar body
senses.definitionCN: 一种为降落到月球、行星等天体表面并完好停留而设计的航天器
senses.example: The lander touched down near the rim of a crater.
senses.exampleCN: 着陆器在环形山边缘附近安全着地。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er marks the thing that performs the action of landing, so any machine whose job is to land is naturally a lander.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 表示「执行动作者」，所以凡是任务就是「落地」的机器，都可以叫作 lander。

senses.title: A person who settles on land
senses.titleCN: 占地定居者：来到某片土地上生活的人
senses.definition: a person who comes to a place and settles on the land, especially one who takes up land to farm or colonize
senses.definitionCN: 来到某地并在土地上定居的人，尤指开垦、耕种或移居开拓的人
senses.example: Early landers cleared the woods and built farms along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的定居者砍伐树林，在河边建起了农场。
senses.why: Long before spaceflight, lander meant someone who comes onto land to stay, because the verb land already meant to come to shore or settle.
senses.whyCN: 在航天时代之前，lander 早已指「上岸留下来的人」，因为动词 land 本就有靠岸、定居的意思。

senses.title: A hard fall or arrival
senses.titleCN: 重重落地：摔下来的一记落点
senses.definition: an informal name for a heavy fall, jolt, or sudden arrival on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对重重摔倒、猛地震到地上或突然落地的说法
senses.example: He took a nasty lander on the ice and bruised his hip.
senses.exampleCN: 他在冰面上狠狠摔了一跤，髋部淤青了。
senses.why: When landing is rough and sudden, the same suffix turns the action into the thing itself, so people joke about taking a big lander.
senses.whyCN: 当着陆又重又突然时，同一个后缀把动作变成了那个「落地的动作本身」，于是口语里会说吃了一记重重落地。

senses.title: A boat that comes ashore
senses.titleCN: 靠岸的船：收帆进港的水上工具
senses.definition: a boat or craft designed or used for reaching the shore, as in old sailing and fishing usage
senses.definitionCN: 为靠岸、上岸而设计或使用的小船，见于旧时航海与渔业用法
senses.example: The fishermen hauled their lander onto the shingle beach.
senses.exampleCN: 渔民们把靠岸的小船拖上卵石滩。
senses.why: Because land once meant to come to shore, anything that lands, including a boat, could be called a lander in port speech.
senses.whyCN: 因为 land 曾表示「靠岸」，凡是能上岸的东西，包括船，在港口口语里都可能被称为 lander。

intro.en: Lander is simply the verb land plus the agent suffix -er, a native English formation whose space sense appeared only in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: lander 就是动词 land 加施事后缀 -er 构成的英语本土派生词，其中「着陆器」的含义直到二十世纪才出现。

items.en: Land meant ground or territory, a word shared with other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古英语 land 指土地、领土，这个词在日耳曼诸语言中同源共用。

items.en: The verb landen appears, meaning to come to shore or reach ground.
items.cn: 动词 landen 出现，意思是靠岸或到达地面。

items.en: Lander names people who come ashore to settle, and later boats that put in to land.
items.cn: lander 指上岸定居的人，后来也指靠岸的船。

items.en: The suffix -er extends the word to any person or thing that lands.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 把词义扩展到任何落地的人或物。

items.en: With spaceflight, lander becomes the standard term for a craft that sets down on another world.
items.cn: 随着航天兴起，lander 成为降落在其他天体上的航天器的标准说法。

note.en: Lander sits in the land family, next to landing, land, and spacecraft words such as rover and probe.
note.cn: lander 属于 land 这一词族，与 landing、land 相邻，也和 rover、probe 等航天器词同场。

entries.definition: the act of coming down to the ground
entries.definitionCN: 降落；着陆（同一词根的动作名词）

entries.definition: to come down to a surface
entries.definitionCN: 落地；着陆（基础动词）

entries.definition: having reached land or settled on it
entries.definitionCN: 已落地的；拥有土地的（同一词根的分词形容词）

entries.definition: a vehicle that moves across the surface of another world
entries.definitionCN: 在其他天体表面移动的巡视车

entries.definition: an unmanned craft sent to explore space
entries.definitionCN: 被送往太空探测的无人航天器

entries.definition: a self-contained part of a spacecraft
entries.definitionCN: 航天器中可独立运作的舱段

normalIntro.en: Lander is the one that lands: the suffix -er always points to the doer of the action.
normalIntro.cn: lander 就是「去落地的那一位」：后缀 -er 永远指向动作的执行者。

normal.en: To land is the verb, and lander is the doer, just as to teach makes teacher.
normal.cn: land 是动词，lander 是执行这个动作的东西，就像 teach 变 teacher。

normal.en: A lunar lander sets down on the Moon, a Mars lander on Mars.
normal.cn: lunar lander 落在月球，Mars lander 落在火星。

normal.en: Lander and landing differ: landing is the act, lander is the craft.
normal.cn: lander 与 landing 不同：landing 是动作，lander 是那个装置。

normal.en: The agent suffix -er also builds rover, explorer, and guide.
normal.cn: 施事后缀 -er 同样构成 rover、explorer、guide。

normal.en: Compare lander with land: the shorter word tells you the action, the longer one tells you who or what does it.
normal.cn: 对比 land 与 lander：短词讲动作，长词讲执行动作的人或物。

abstract.en: Imagine a metal insect with three legs easing itself down onto grey dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一只三条腿的金属昆虫，缓缓把身体压到灰色尘土上。

abstract.en: Picture a family arriving on a new shore, setting down bundles and calling it home.
abstract.cn: 想象一家人来到新的海岸，放下行囊，就把这里称作家。

abstract.en: Feel the thump of a body hitting the floor after a slip.
abstract.cn: 感受滑倒之后身体砸在地面上那一声闷响。

examples.en: The lander sent back the first close images of the surface.
examples.cn: 着陆器传回了第一张表面的近距离图像。

examples.en: Engineers tested the lander legs on a bed of crushed rock.
examples.cn: 工程师在碎石床上测试了着陆器的支腿。

examples.en: A good lander must slow down before it ever touches the ground.
examples.cn: 好的着陆器必须在触地之前就把速度降下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「懒的」——探测器懒得飞了，就找块地赖着不走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 land（土地）→ 中古英语 landen（上岸、落地）→ land + -er（执行动作者）→ lander：靠岸的船或人 → 二十世纪航天用语中的「着陆器」。

sensesIntro.en: Lander starts as someone who comes ashore to settle, moves to boats that put in to land, and in modern use becomes the craft that lands on another world.
sensesIntro.cn: lander 最初指上岸定居的人，继而指靠岸的船，现代又专指着陆在其他世界上的航天器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a craft pressing its legs down onto an unfamiliar surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台飞行器把支腿压在陌生的地面上。

branches.en: The spacecraft sense is the modern mainstream meaning.
branches.cn: 航天器义是现代最主流的用法。

branches.en: The settler sense keeps the oldest human side of landing.
branches.cn: 定居者义保留了「落地」最早的人类含义。

branches.en: The informal fall sense turns landing into a jolt.
branches.cn: 口语中的摔跤义把落地变成了一记撞击。

branches.en: A lander in space and a lander in a harbour are both things made to arrive safely.
branches.cn: 太空中的着陆器与港口的靠岸小船都是为安全抵达而造。

branches.en: Both a settler and a boat bring people onto the shore to stay.
branches.cn: 定居者与靠岸的船都把人和土地连接起来，让人留下来。

intro.en: Lander is built from the native base land with the agent suffix -er, the same pattern as teacher and builder.
intro.cn: lander 由本土基础词 land 加施事后缀 -er 构成，与 teacher、builder 的构词模式相同。

latinIntro.en: Land is Germanic in origin and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries here are a later learned borrowing of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: land 源于日耳曼语系，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁说法只是后世对英语词的学术借译。

items.example: The base word land means ground or territory.
items.exampleCN: 基础词 land 意为土地或陆地。

items.example: The verb land means to reach the ground.
items.exampleCN: 动词 land 意为抵达地面。

items.example: The suffix -er turns land into lander.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 land 变成 lander。

items.example: Teacher shows the same agent pattern.
items.exampleCN: teacher 展示了同样的施事构词。

items.example: Builder is built the same way as lander.
items.exampleCN: builder 与 lander 构词方式相同。

items.example: Landing names the act that the lander performs.
items.exampleCN: landing 命名了 lander 所执行的动作。

items.example: Landed marks the finished act of landing.
items.exampleCN: landed 标记已完成的落地动作。

items.meaning: a vehicle that roams a surface
items.example: Rover is the moving partner of a lander.
items.exampleCN: rover 是着陆器的移动搭档。

latinEntries.meaning: to make earthy or shaped like earth
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使成土状（与 terra 土地同源，仅供对照）

definition_zh: 垃圾填埋场；填埋；废物填埋处理
definition_en: a large area of land where waste is buried in layers under soil, or the method of burying waste in this way
core_image: 一铲一铲的垃圾被推进深坑，推土机压平，再盖上一层黄土
scene: 城郊那处旧采石坑被一层层垃圾和泥土填平，最后盖上草皮。Trucks keep dumping rubbish at the landfill outside town.
sceneCN: 这里 landfill 是「垃圾填埋场」（第 1 个义项：把垃圾层层埋进土里的场地）；句意为卡车不断把垃圾倒进城外的填埋场。

pos.zh: 垃圾填埋场（可数）；填埋、垃圾填埋处理（不可数）
填埋；以填埋方式处理（较少用）

collocations.zh: 填埋气（垃圾腐烂产生的甲烷）

derivatives.zh: 倾倒场、垃圾场：常与填埋场混用，但 dump 强调随意倾倒，未必有覆盖土层
landfill 的后项，意为「填满」，也是全词的字面来源
卫生填埋：在填埋场底部加防渗层、每日覆土的工程化填埋方式

senses.title: A site where waste is buried
senses.titleCN: 垃圾填埋场：层层埋压垃圾的场地
senses.definition: a site where household or industrial waste is buried in layers and covered with earth
senses.definitionCN: 把生活垃圾或工业废物分层埋入并覆土的场地
senses.example: The old quarry became a landfill after it closed.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧采石场关闭后变成了垃圾填埋场。
senses.why: Land supplies the ground and fill supplies the action of filling, so a landfill is literally land that has been filled in with waste.
senses.whyCN: land 提供「土地」，fill 提供「填满」的动作，所以 landfill 字面上就是「被垃圾填起来的土地」。

senses.title: The practice of burying waste
senses.titleCN: 填埋处理：把垃圾埋起来的做法
senses.definition: the method or practice of disposing of waste by burying it in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 用把废物埋入地下的方式来处置废物的方法或做法
senses.example: The council wants to cut how much waste goes to landfill.
senses.exampleCN: 市政当局想减少送往填埋的垃圾量。
senses.why: Once a site is named, the word can name the method itself, so sending waste to landfill means disposing of it this way.
senses.whyCN: 场地被命名之后，这个词也能指方法本身，所以「送往填埋」就是按这种方式处理垃圾。

senses.title: The material itself
senses.titleCN: 挖掘填筑的土石：用作填方的土料
senses.definition: earth, rubble, or other material used to raise or level the ground in construction
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑中用来抬高或整平地面的土、碎石等材料
senses.example: Engineers used rubble as landfill to raise the road above the flood line.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用碎石做了填方，把路面抬到洪水线以上。
senses.why: The older civil-engineering sense comes first: fill is material dug from one place and moved to fill another, so landfill means fill land.
senses.whyCN: 最早的土木工程义反而更早：fill 指从一处挖出、填到另一处的土料，所以 landfill 就是「用土石去填地」。

senses.title: A capped, reclaimed area
senses.titleCN: 封场复垦的填埋区：封盖后另作他用
senses.definition: a former burial site that has been sealed with a cap and turned into a park, sports field, or other new use
senses.definitionCN: 已用封顶层密封，并改造成公园、运动场或其他用途的旧填埋场地
senses.example: The capped landfill is now a grassy hill with a running track.
senses.exampleCN: 封场后的填埋场如今是一座带跑道的草坡。
senses.why: Modern regulations let a full site be sealed and reused, so the word also names the reclaimed form rather than only the dumping phase.
senses.whyCN: 现代法规允许填满的场地封盖后重新利用，所以该词也可以指复垦后的形态，而不仅指倒垃圾的阶段。

intro.en: Landfill joins the native land with fill, a word of Old English origin, and first served civil engineering before it named waste disposal.
intro.cn: landfill 由本土词 land 与源自古英语的 fill 组合而成，最早服务于土木工程，后来才用来指废物处置。

items.en: Land means ground, and fyllan means to make full.
items.cn: 古英语 land 指土地，fyllan 意为使满。

items.en: Landfill appears in earthworks, meaning soil used to raise or level ground.
items.cn: landfill 在土方工程中出现，指尖土或填方所用土料。

items.en: Landfill appears in earthworks, meaning soil used to raise or level ground.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，城市工程人员开始用洼地和坑洼作为倾倒垃圾的场地。

items.en: Landfill shifts from the material to the waste burial site itself.
items.cn: landfill 由指土料转向指垃圾填埋场地本身。

items.en: With waste regulations, landfill names both the place and the practice of burying waste.
items.cn: 随着废物法规出台，landfill 同时指填埋场所与填埋这种做法。

note.en: Landfill belongs to the land compounds and to the family of waste-disposal words such as dump, tip, and incinerator.
note.cn: landfill 属于 land 构成的复合词，也属于 dump、tip、incinerator 等废物处置词场。

entries.definition: to make something full
entries.definitionCN: 使……满；填满（复合词后半部分）

entries.definition: methane released by rotting waste in a landfill
entries.definitionCN: 填埋场中垃圾腐烂释放的甲烷

entries.definition: an owner who lets out property
entries.definitionCN: 房东；地主（同为 land 开头的复合词）

entries.definition: a place where rubbish is left
entries.definitionCN: 垃圾倾倒场；垃圾场

entries.definition: a place where waste is tipped and buried
entries.definitionCN: 垃圾倾倒场（英式用法）

entries.definition: a plant that burns waste
entries.definitionCN: 焚烧垃圾的设施

normalIntro.en: Landfill is a picture word: land plus a hole that gets filled with rubbish.
normalIntro.cn: landfill 是个画面词：land 加一个被垃圾填满的坑。

normal.en: Fill means to make full, so landfill is land filled up with waste.
normal.cn: fill 意为填满，所以 landfill 就是被垃圾填起来的土地。

normal.en: Compare landfill with landform: one is made by people, the other by nature.
normal.cn: 对比 landfill 与 landform：一个由人造，一个由自然形成。

normal.en: British people often say tip for a landfill site.
normal.cn: 英国人口语里常用 tip 指填埋场。

normal.en: The phrase send to landfill shows landfill used as a method, not only a place.
normal.cn: 「送往填埋场」这个说法表明 landfill 也可指一种处理方式，而不只是地点。

normal.en: Landfill gas is methane released as buried waste rots.
normal.cn: landfill gas 是埋着的垃圾腐烂时释放的甲烷。

abstract.en: Picture a hill that is really a flattened pile of rubbish under turf.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小山，其实是草皮下一层压平的垃圾。

abstract.en: Watch a bulldozer pack a fresh layer, then a soil spreader cover it.
abstract.cn: 想象推土机压实新的一层垃圾，撒土机随即盖上一层土。

abstract.en: See a quarry pit slowly turning into a level field.
abstract.cn: 想象一处采石坑慢慢被填成一块平地。

examples.en: The landfill will reach capacity in about five years.
examples.cn: 这座填埋场大约五年后就会填满。

examples.en: Food waste in landfill produces methane for decades.
examples.cn: 埋进填埋场的厨余垃圾会持续几十年产生甲烷。

examples.en: Recycling keeps cardboard out of the landfill.
examples.cn: 回收让纸板免于进入填埋场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「烂地费力」——把垃圾埋进烂地，每一车都很费力；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 land（土地）+ fyllan（使满）→ fill（填满）→ 英语 landfill：土木工程中的「填方土料」→ 现代指「垃圾填埋场、填埋处理」。

sensesIntro.en: Landfill moves from engineering material for raising ground, to a site for buried waste, to the practice of disposing waste that way, and finally to the reclaimed land.
sensesIntro.cn: landfill 从抬高地面的填方材料，变为埋垃圾的场地，再变为这种处置方式，最后也可指封场后复垦的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pit filled layer by layer with rubbish and soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个坑被垃圾和土一层层填满。

branches.en: The site sense is the most common meaning today.
branches.cn: 场地义是今天最常见的用法。

branches.en: The practice sense is what sending waste to landfill refers to.
branches.cn: 把垃圾送往填埋场指的就是填埋这种处理方式。

branches.en: The earthwork sense is the oldest, about soil that fills land.
branches.cn: 土方义最古老，指尖方、填地的土石材料。

branches.en: The place and the method share the same buried layers.
branches.cn: 场地与方法共享同一层层埋压的动作。

branches.en: A sealed site can become a park, so a dump turns into a green hill.
branches.cn: 封场的场地可变成公园，垃圾场因此化为绿坡。

intro.en: Landfill is a native compound of land and fill, with no borrowed suffix.
intro.cn: landfill 是 land 与 fill 构成的本土复合词，不含借入的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Both parts of landfill are Germanic; there is no Latin ancestor, and the Latin list gives only distant relatives of land for comparison.
latinIntro.cn: landfill 的两个部分都属日耳曼语系，没有拉丁语祖先；下面只列出与「土地」概念相关的远亲，供对照。

items.example: Land is the ground being filled.
items.exampleCN: land 是被填起来的那块地。

items.example: Fill carries the action in the compound.
items.exampleCN: fill 承担了复合词里的动作。

items.example: Landslide is another common land compound.
items.exampleCN: landslide 是另一个常见的 land 复合词。

items.example: Landform combines land with form.
items.exampleCN: landform 是 land 与 form 的组合。

items.example: Landscape uses land plus a borrowed suffix.
items.exampleCN: landscape 是 land 加借入后缀构成。

items.example: Landlord uses the same first part.
items.exampleCN: landlord 使用同一个起首部分。

items.example: Refill adds the prefix re- to fill.
items.exampleCN: refill 在 fill 前加了前缀 re-。

items.example: Filling shares the action of fill.
items.exampleCN: filling 与 fill 共享「填」的动作。

items.example: Dump is the older everyday word for such places.
items.exampleCN: dump 是这类场地更早的日常说法。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 土地；大地（仅供「土地」概念对照）
填满；充满（仅供「填满」概念对照）

definition_zh: 地标；著名建筑；里程碑；分水岭事件；界标
definition_en: a building or feature easily seen and used to identify a place, or an event marking an important change
core_image: 远处山顶立着一块刻字的界石，走在哪儿的人一抬头都看得见
scene: 旅人在陌生街道上抬头看见那座高塔，一下就知道自己在哪。The tower has been a landmark for sailors for centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 landmark 是「地标」（第 1 个义项：容易辨认、用来定位的建筑物或景物）；句意为这座塔数百年来一直是水手认路的标志。

pos.zh: 地标；界标；里程碑（可数，复数 landmarks）
里程碑式的；标志性的（仅作定语）

derivatives.zh: landmark 的后项，原指界标、标记，也是全词的字面来源
landmark 加 -ing 的派生名词：以地标进行定位或标记的做法
landmark 加 -ed 的派生形容词：被列为受保护地标的

senses.title: A feature that guides the eye
senses.titleCN: 地标：易于辨认、用于定位的景物
senses.definition: a building, hill, or other feature that is easy to see and used to tell where you are
senses.definitionCN: 高大、醒目、容易看见并用来判断所在位置的建筑、山丘或其他景物
senses.example: From the harbour the white cliff is the best landmark.
senses.exampleCN: 从港口望去，那道白崖是最好的定位标志。
senses.why: Land gives the place and mark gives the sign, so a landmark is literally the mark on the land that tells you where you stand.
senses.whyCN: land 给出地点，mark 给出记号，所以 landmark 字面上就是「打在土地上的记号」，用来说明你身在何处。

senses.title: A boundary stone
senses.titleCN: 界标：划出地块边界的石块
senses.definition: a stone or post that marks the boundary of a piece of land or a property
senses.definitionCN: 标出某块土地或产业边界的石块或木桩
senses.example: Farmers rebuilt the landmark where their fields meet.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们重立了田块交界处的界石。
senses.why: The oldest use is a physical stone marking where one land ends, which gives the whole word its concrete, settling quality.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法就是一块实实在在的石头，标明一块地到哪里为止，这给全词打下了具体、确定的底色。

senses.title: A turning point in history
senses.titleCN: 里程碑：标志重大转变的事件或成果
senses.definition: an event, achievement, or work that marks an important stage or turning point
senses.definitionCN: 标志重要阶段或转折点的事件、成就或作品
senses.example: The first published dictionary was a landmark in English learning.
senses.exampleCN: 第一部出版的词典是英语学习的一座里程碑。
senses.why: A stone that marks a boundary extends easily into a mark that divides one era from the next, so a big event becomes a landmark.
senses.whyCN: 划出边界的石头，很容易引申为划开两个时代的记号，于是重大事件就成了里程碑。

senses.title: A legally protected place
senses.titleCN: 受保护的历史地标：被官方认定的建筑
senses.definition: a building or site that is officially listed as worthy of preservation because of its history or architecture
senses.definitionCN: 因历史或建筑价值而被官方列入名单、应予保护的建筑或场所
senses.example: The station was designated a landmark last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这座车站去年被认定为历史地标。
senses.why: When marking becomes an official act, the word moves from what the eye sees to what the law protects.
senses.whyCN: 当「标记」变成官方行为时，这个词就从眼睛看见的东西转到法律保护的东西。

intro.en: Landmark is a native English compound of land and mark, and its history runs from a boundary stone to a symbol of change.
intro.cn: landmark 是由 land 与 mark 构成的本土英语复合词，其历史从一块界石一路走到「变革的象征」。

items.en: Land means ground and mearc means a boundary or sign.
items.cn: 古英语 land 指土地，mearc 指边界或记号。

items.en: Landmearc appears for a boundary marker between estates.
items.cn: landmearc 已见于文献，指庄园之间划界的标记。

items.en: The form becomes landmark and still means a boundary object.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 landmark，仍指划界的物件。

items.en: Sailors and travellers use landmark for any object that helps them judge position.
items.cn: 水手与旅人用 landmark 指任何有助于判断方位的东西。

items.en: The figurative sense of an important turning point becomes common in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪，「里程碑、转折点」的比喻义变得普遍。

note.en: Landmark sits among land compounds, and among words for guideposts, turning points, and famous sights.
note.cn: landmark 与 land 类复合词相邻，也与各类「路标、转折点、名胜」词同场。

entries.definition: a sign or spot used to identify something
entries.definitionCN: 用作识别依据的记号（复合词后半部分）

entries.definition: the act of using landmarks to fix position
entries.definitionCN: 借助地标确定位置的做法

entries.definition: a natural feature of the land
entries.definitionCN: 地貌；地表形态（同为 land 开头的复合词）

entries.definition: a structure built to remember a person or event
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念人物或事件而建的建筑物

entries.definition: an event marking an important stage
entries.definitionCN: 标志重要阶段的里程碑事件

entries.definition: a light or tower that guides travellers
entries.definitionCN: 为旅人导航的灯或塔

normalIntro.en: Landmark is the mark on the land: two short native words pressed together.
normalIntro.cn: landmark 就是「土地上的记号」：两个简短的本土词压在一起。

normal.en: Land means ground, and a landmark is a mark on that ground.
normal.cn: land 指土地，landmark 就是打在这块土地上的记号。

normal.en: Old English mearc meant a boundary, which survives in the second part of landmark.
normal.cn: 古英语 mearc 意为边界，这一含义保留在 landmark 的后半部分里。

normal.en: A landmark decision is a decision that changes how things are done.
normal.cn: landmark decision 指改变做事方式的标志性裁决。

normal.en: Compare landmark with milestone: both mark progress, but a milestone is abstract, a landmark is a place.
normal.cn: 对比 landmark 与 milestone：两者都标志进展，但 milestone 更抽象，landmark 更具体。

normal.en: In tourism, a landmark is the spot people photograph first.
normal.cn: 在旅游语境里，landmark 是人们最先拍照的那个地方。

abstract.en: See a stone on a hilltop, visible from every road below.
abstract.cn: 想象山顶上一块石头，山下的每条路都看得见它。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer tapping a boundary stone with a stick to settle a dispute.
abstract.cn: 想象农夫用木棍敲敲界石，以此平息一场争执。

abstract.en: Think of a film poster with a bold line drawn across it in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张电影海报，中间被画上一条粗重的分界线。

examples.en: The bridge is a famous landmark in the old town.
examples.cn: 这座桥是旧城著名的地标。

examples.en: Her discovery became a landmark in modern medicine.
examples.cn: 她的发现成为现代医学的一座里程碑。

examples.en: Pilots use landmarks to check their position on long flights.
examples.cn: 飞行员在长途飞行中借助地标核对位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蓝的马克」——在地图上用蓝色马克笔圈出的那块石头，就是地标；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 land（土地）+ mearc（边界、记号）→ 中古英语 landmark（界石）→ 英语：可辨认的景物、地标 → 引申为「里程碑、转折点」。

sensesIntro.en: Landmark starts as a boundary stone, becomes any visible feature that fixes your position, and then extends to events and protected buildings that mark a line in life or history.
sensesIntro.cn: landmark 起初是划界的石头，继而成为任何帮你确定位置的显眼景物，再引申为在生活或历史上划出分界的事件与受保护建筑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked stone on the land, visible from far away.
core.cn: 核心意象：土地上一块带着记号、远远就能看见的石头。

branches.en: The guiding-feature sense is the everyday one.
branches.cn: 用于定位的景物义是日常用法。

branches.en: The boundary stone is the oldest concrete sense.
branches.cn: 界石义是最古老的具体含义。

branches.en: The turning-point sense takes the boundary idea into time.
branches.cn: 里程碑义把「边界」的想法搬进了时间维度。

branches.en: A building can first be seen as scenery and later be listed for protection.
branches.cn: 一座建筑可以先作为景物被看见，之后又被列入保护名单。

branches.en: Both a boundary stone and a landmark event divide one thing from another.
branches.cn: 界石与里程碑事件都把前与后分隔开来。

intro.en: Landmark is a native compound, with land as the place and mark as the old word for boundary or sign.
intro.cn: landmark 是本土复合词：land 是地点，mark 是古代表示「边界、记号」的旧词。

latinIntro.en: Both land and mark are Germanic; Old English mearc is related to Latin margo, a border, which survives in English margin.
latinIntro.cn: land 与 mark 都属日耳曼语系；古英语 mearc 与拉丁语 margo（边缘）相关，后者在英语中留下 margin。

items.example: Mark supplies the visible sign.
items.exampleCN: mark 提供看得见的记号。

items.example: Landform puts land first in the same way.

items.exampleCN: marker 重复了「做记号」的意思。

definition_zh: 朝陆地的；向陆的；内陆一侧的；向陆地方向
definition_en: towards the land or the interior of a country, especially as seen from the sea or from a river mouth
core_image: 站在甲板上的人背对大海，眼睛望向岸上一排灰色的屋顶
scene: 货船缓缓驶进港湾，甲板上的水手回头望向岸上那排灰屋顶，那里就是家的方向。From the deck the sailors watched the landward slope of the coast turn green and gold at sunset.
sceneCN: 这里 landward 表示「朝陆地的一侧」，属于第 1 个义项（形容词：朝陆地的、向陆的）；句意为：水手们站在甲板上，望着海岸朝陆地那面山坡在落日里变成绿色与金色。

pos.zh: 朝陆地的；向陆的；内陆一侧的
向陆地；朝内陆

collocations.phrase: the landward edge of the marsh

derivatives.zh: 在 landward 后加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向陆地」
短语用法，义为「在……靠陆地的一侧」
复合名词，指沼泽、滩涂或盐沼靠陆地的那条边缘

senses.title: Facing the land
senses.definition: facing or directed towards the land rather than towards the sea
senses.definitionCN: 面向或朝向陆地，而不是朝向海面
senses.example: The landward side of the lighthouse wall was covered with ivy.
senses.exampleCN: 灯塔墙靠陆地的那一面爬满了常春藤。
senses.why: The second element means direction, so the word names whichever side turns towards the shore.
senses.whyCN: 后半个成分表示「方向」，所以这个词指的就是转向岸边的那一面。

senses.title: Moving towards the interior
senses.definition: moving from a coast or river edge towards the inside of the country
senses.definitionCN: 从海岸或河岸一带朝内地移动
senses.example: Storm waves pushed the shingle landward and buried the path.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴掀起的海浪把砾石推向陆地，把小路都埋住了。
senses.why: Once the side is named, a direction of travel along that side follows naturally.
senses.whyCN: 既然定下了陆地那一侧，顺着这一侧行进的方向也就自然成立了。

senses.title: On the shore side of a structure
senses.definition: situated on the part of a pier, harbour or wall that is nearest the shore
senses.definitionCN: 位于码头、港口或堤墙离岸边最近的那一部分
senses.example: Buses stop at the landward end of the pier, where the pavement begins.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车停在码头靠陆地的那一端，人行道就是从这里开始的。
senses.why: A structure has a sea end and a shore end, and this word marks the shore end.
senses.whyCN: 结构总有临海一端和靠岸一端，这个词专门标出靠岸的那一端。

senses.title: Taken on the land rather than at sea
senses.definition: happening on land, or described as observed from the land, not from the water
senses.definitionCN: 发生在陆地上，或从陆地而不是从水面观察到的
senses.example: Coastal farms suffered from the landward wind and the salt it carried.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海的农场深受来自陆地一侧的风以及风中盐分的伤害。
senses.why: If land is the point of view, then anything seen or felt from that point takes the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然以陆地为观察点，那么从这一侧看到或感到的都能用上这个词。

senses.title: Inland as a place
senses.definition: the parts of a country away from its sea coast or from a great river
senses.definitionCN: 一国远离海岸或远离大河的区域
senses.example: Families from the landward villages walk to the market on the coast each week.
senses.exampleCN: 内陆村庄的人家每周都走到海边集市上去。
senses.why: The same direction, read as a whole area, turns into inland country.
senses.whyCN: 同一个方向，若把它当作一片区域来读，就变成了内陆腹地。

senses.title: Further from the open sea
senses.definition: used to place something further inland than another thing mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 用来指比提到的另一物更靠内陆的位置
senses.example: The landward basin is quieter than the quay where the ferries load.
senses.exampleCN: 靠内陆那边的港湾比渡船装货的码头安静得多。
senses.why: The word also ranks places, so one bay can stand further landward than another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词还能给地点排序，因此一个港湾可以比另一个更靠陆地方向。

senses.title: The direction of a stream or tide
senses.definition: used of water that moves from the sea into an estuary or from the coast into the tidal flats
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述从海面进入河口、或从海岸涌向潮滩的水
senses.example: At flood tide the current runs landward through the narrow channel.
senses.exampleCN: 涨潮时，水流顺着狭窄的航道朝陆地涌去。
senses.why: Tide and current also have two directions, and the sea direction and the shore direction are named by this word and its twin.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐和水流同样有两个方向，朝岸和朝海分别由这个词及其对应词来表达。

senses.title: Aiming a light or signal to shore
senses.titleCN: 把灯光或信号指向岸上
senses.definition: directed from a ship, raft or deep-water platform towards the shore
senses.definitionCN: 从船、筏或深水平台指向岸上
senses.example: The crew turned the searchlight landward to signal the harbour office.
senses.exampleCN: 船员把探照灯转向岸上，给港务办公室发信号。
senses.why: Signals travel in a named direction, so the word easily describes beams and calls aimed at shore.
senses.whyCN: 信号总是朝着某个方向发出，于是这个词也能描述照向岸边或喊向岸上的光束与呼唤。

intro.en: Landward joins land, an old Germanic word for ground or territory, with ward, a directional suffix from an Old English element that grew out of a root for watching and turning towards.
intro.cn: landward 由两部分组成：land 是表示「土地、疆域」的古老日耳曼词；ward 来自古英语中表示方向的后缀成分，其更早的词根与「看守、转向」有关。

items.en: A reconstructed noun meaning land or territory lies behind both English land and its German and Dutch cousins.
items.cn: 一个表示「土地、疆域」的日耳曼语重构名词，是英语 land 以及德语、荷兰语同族词的共同来源。

items.en: Waru meant guard, care or shelter, and a related form turned the idea of watching into a sense of direction towards.
items.cn: 古英语 waru 意为看守、照料或庇护；与之相关的形式把「看守」的意思引申为朝向某方。

items.en: Landward appears as an adverb of direction meaning towards the land, much as homeward means towards home.
items.cn: 古英语中已有表示方向的副词形式，意为朝向陆地，构词方式与 homeward 表示朝家而去相同。

items.en: The adverb ending alternated between ward and wards, giving two spellings of one word that still both survive.
items.cn: 副词词尾在 ward 与 wards 之间交替，形成同一词的两个拼法，至今两者并存。

items.en: Sailing and map writing gave the word a fixed place next to its twin seaward in descriptions of coasts.
items.cn: 航海与制图使这个词在与 seaward 这一对应词的对照中固定下来，专门用于描写海岸。

items.en: Today it serves ecology, geography and planning, and it is also used as an adjective before words like side and slope.
items.cn: 今天它服务于生态学、地理学与规划文本，也常作形容词放在 side、slope 这类词之前。

note.en: The first group shares the directional element ward; the second group gathers other words for the shore and for the interior.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示方向的后缀 ward；第二组收集与岸边、内陆有关的其他说法。

entries.definition: towards the sea rather than towards the land
entries.definitionCN: 朝海的、向海的，与这个词方向相反。

entries.definition: towards the inside of something
entries.definitionCN: 向内的，共享同一个方向后缀。

entries.definition: towards home
entries.definitionCN: 朝家的、向家的，构词方式完全相同。

entries.definition: in the direction of
entries.definitionCN: 朝向，其中的方向成分与本词同源。

entries.definition: the inner part of a country, away from the sea
entries.definitionCN: 内陆；内地的，与朝陆地方向的意思接近。

entries.definition: towards or on the land from the sea
entries.definitionCN: 向岸的；在岸上的，方向感相近。

entries.definition: towards the shore
entries.definitionCN: 朝岸的，方向相近但更强调岸线本身。

normalIntro.en: Landward is simply land plus the direction suffix ward, the same suffix that builds homeward and seaward.
normalIntro.cn: landward 就是 land 加上表示方向的后缀 ward，homeward 与 seaward 用的是同一个后缀。

normal.en: Land plus ward: ward marks direction, so the whole word means the way towards land.
normal.cn: land 加 ward：ward 标方向，合起来就是朝陆地的方向。

normal.en: Its twin seaward uses the same suffix, so the two words face each other across the coastline.
normal.cn: 它的对应词 seaward 用同一个后缀，两词隔着海岸线相对而立。

normal.en: The adverb form allows the ending s as well, which is why both spellings are correct.
normal.cn: 副词形式还可以加 s 结尾，因此两种拼法都正确。

normal.en: The landward side of anything means the side you meet first when you come from the sea.
normal.cn: 任何事物的 landward side 都指从海上来时最先碰到的那一面。

normal.en: Compare inland: inland names a place, while this word points in a direction.
normal.cn: 对比 inland：inland 指一处地方，而这个词指向一个方向。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pointing from the water towards dry ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指从水面指向干燥的地面。

abstract.en: Think of a wave running up the beach until it has nowhere left to go.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪冲上沙滩，直到它再也无处可去。

abstract.en: See a small boat turning its light from the dark water towards the lit windows on shore.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小船把灯从黑暗的水面转向岸上亮着的窗户。

examples.en: The landward side of the island is sheltered from the worst storms.
examples.cn: 岛靠陆地的那一侧能避开最猛的风暴。

examples.en: Sand is being carried landward by the rising tide.
examples.cn: 沙子正被上涨的潮水带向陆地。

examples.en: Each evening the crews walk landward along the pier to the bus stop.
examples.cn: 每天傍晚船员们沿着码头朝陆地走到公交站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「land + ward」——「懒得的」人往岸上走，land 是陆地，ward 是朝向：朝陆地；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 land（土地、疆域）来自日耳曼语系的 land；ward 来自古英语中表示方向的成分，其更早形式与 waru（看守、照料）相关，引申为「朝向」。两者合成后指「朝陆地的」，与 homeward、seaward 构词方式一致。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a shore-facing surface, to movement towards the interior, a structure shore end, a land viewpoint, inland country, a further-from-sea position, water direction and signals aimed at shore.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项依次展开：朝陆地的面、向内地移动、结构靠岸一端、以陆地为观察点、内陆地区、离外海更远的位置、水流的陆向以及指向岸上的灯光信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sailor on deck with his back to the open sea, eyes on a row of grey roofs.
core.cn: 核心意象：甲板上的水手背对大海，眼睛望向一排灰色屋顶。

branches.en: THE SHORE FACE OF THINGS: a side, an end or a wall that looks towards land.
branches.cn: 事物的朝岸面：朝向陆地的那一面、那一端或那堵墙。

branches.en: MOVEMENT TOWARDS LAND: waves, wind, sand and even light travel in this direction.
branches.cn: 朝向陆地的运动：浪、风、沙乃至光线都朝这个方向。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION UNDER WATCH: water and wind are tracked through a seaward and a landward phase.
branches.cn: 被观察的方向：水流与风被分成朝海与朝陆两个阶段来记录。

branches.en: LAND AS A PLACE: the same direction read as a whole region turns into the inland country.
branches.cn: 作为地点的陆地：把同一方向当成一整片区域来读，就是内陆腹地。

branches.en: DISTANCE FROM OPEN WATER: the shoreward basin is quieter than the working quay.
branches.cn: 与外水的距离：靠岸的港湾比忙碌的码头安静。

intro.en: This is a native English compound: the noun land plus the directional suffix ward, with no Latin root involved.
intro.cn: 这是一个英语本土复合词：名词 land 加表示方向的后缀 ward，不涉及拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin relatives, so the list of Latin entries is empty for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁同源词，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Land names the goal of the direction.
items.exampleCN: land 指明方向所指向的目标。

items.example: The suffix turns a place into a direction of travel.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把地点变成行进的方向。

items.example: The s ending gives the adverb form of the same word.
items.exampleCN: 加 s 的词尾给出同一个词的副词形式。

items.example: It is the exact opposite of this word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词完全相反的方向词。

items.example: It shows the same building pattern.
items.exampleCN: 它展示了相同的构词方式。

items.example: The suffix also marks inner direction here.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀在这里同样标记向内的方向。

items.example: It sets an inward direction against an outward one.
items.exampleCN: 它把向内的方向与向外的方向对照起来。

items.example: The prefix in- replaces ward as the direction marker.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 替代 ward 充当方向标记。

items.example: It points at the shoreline instead of the country side.
items.exampleCN: 它指向岸线，而不是内陆一侧。

items.example: It is the adverb twin of this adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个形容词的副词对应形式。

短语用法，义为「在……靠陆地的一侧」
复合名词，指盐沼或滩涂靠陆地的边缘

definition_zh: 盗窃罪；窃盗；非暴力的侵占他人财产罪
definition_en: the crime of taking and carrying away someone else money or goods without the owner consent, especially without using force
core_image: 有人把别人的钱包塞进自己口袋，脚步轻快，却已经被监控拍下
scene: 法庭上被告低头站着，检察官说明他趁着商店无人注意把整箱货物搬走，这在当地法律里算是盗窃。In many American states, larceny covers both petty theft and grand theft of a large sum.
sceneCN: 这里 larceny 指「盗窃罪」（第 1 个义项：非法拿走他人财物的罪名）；句意为：在美国的许多州里，这个词既包括小额的偷窃，也包括金额巨大的重大盗窃。

pos.zh: 盗窃罪；窃盗；非法侵占他人财物

collocations.zh: 骗取式盗窃（以欺骗手段取得占有）

derivatives.zh: 在 larceny 词根后加形容词词尾 -ous 构成，义为「盗窃的；有偷窃意图的」
在 larcenous 后加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「以偷窃的方式」
在 larceny 词根后加表示人的词尾 -ist 构成，义为「盗窃犯」（军中俚语常用）

senses.title: The legal crime of theft
senses.definition: the offence of taking another person property with the intention of keeping it permanently
senses.definitionCN: 以永久占有为目的取走他人财物的犯罪行为
senses.example: The shop assistant was arrested for larceny after the till was found short.
senses.exampleCN: 收银机里的钱少了，那名店员因盗窃罪被逮捕。
senses.why: The Old French noun meant robbery, and English law kept the word for the taking of goods.
senses.whyCN: 古法语名词本义为抢夺，英语法律沿用这个词来指取走财物。

senses.title: Petty theft
senses.definition: theft of goods of small value, treated as a lesser offence than grand theft
senses.definitionCN: 窃取价值较小的财物，比重大盗窃的量刑更轻
senses.example: Stealing a bottle of wine from a shop may be treated as petty larceny.
senses.exampleCN: 从商店偷一瓶葡萄酒可能被当作轻窃处理。
senses.why: The value of the thing taken sets the label, so a cheap item falls on the lighter side of the line.
senses.whyCN: 被拿走之物的价值决定标签，便宜的东西自然落在界线较轻的一边。

senses.title: Grand theft
senses.definition: theft of goods above a set value, carrying a heavier penalty in law
senses.definitionCN: 窃取超过法定金额的财物，在法律上处罚更重
senses.example: Driving off with a fully loaded truck counted as grand larceny.
senses.exampleCN: 开走一辆装满货物的卡车被算作重大盗窃。
senses.why: Above a fixed sum the same act becomes a graver charge, which is why the scale has two names.
senses.whyCN: 一旦超过法定金额，同样的行为就变成更重的指控，所以这条刻度有两个名字。

senses.title: Taking goods out of another possession
senses.titleCN: 从他人占有中取走财物
senses.definition: the taking and carrying away of property that is in another person control
senses.definitionCN: 把处于他人控制之下的财物取走并带离
senses.example: The court asked whether the goods had left the owner control, which larceny requires.
senses.exampleCN: 法院要查明财物是否已离开物主的控制，这是构成盗窃必须满足的条件。
senses.why: Common law built the crime out of two moves: taking the thing and carrying it away.
senses.whyCN: 普通法把这个罪名拆成两个动作：先取走东西，再把它带离。

senses.title: Theft without force
senses.definition: unlawful taking that does not involve force or threats against a person
senses.definitionCN: 不涉及对人施加暴力或威胁的非法取财行为
senses.example: Unlike robbery, larceny does not require the victim to be threatened or hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 与抢劫不同，盗窃罪的成立并不要求受害者受到威胁或伤害。
senses.why: Lawyers needed a word for quiet taking, so robbery was kept for taking by fear or force.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个词来描述不声不响的取财行为，而抢劫一词留给了靠恐惧或武力实施的夺取。

senses.title: Theft by deception
senses.definition: taking property with the owner consent obtained by fraud or a misleading story
senses.definitionCN: 用欺诈或误导性的说法取得物主同意后拿走财物
senses.example: The man who posed as a meter reader was charged with larceny by trick.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冒充查表员的人被控骗取式盗窃。
senses.why: If consent itself was manufactured by a lie, the law treats the taking as theft.
senses.whyCN: 如果所谓「同意」本身是谎言造出来的，法律就把这种取财视为盗窃。

senses.title: Taking gas or power
senses.definition: the unlawful use of electricity, gas or water supplied to another person
senses.definitionCN: 非法使用供应给他人的电力、燃气或水
senses.example: A modern statute may treat the tapping of a power line as larceny of service.
senses.exampleCN: 现代法规可能把私接电线的行为视为服务类盗窃。
senses.why: Once the object of theft can be measured inside a pipe or a wire, the old crime was stretched to cover it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被盗之物可以被计量，哪怕它藏在管道或电线里，古老的罪名也会被扩展来覆盖它。

senses.title: In military jargon, pilfering
senses.definition: used informally of any small sneaky borrowing among troops, sometimes half joking
senses.definitionCN: 军用口语，指部队里任何偷偷拿走的举动，有时带半开玩笑的语气
senses.example: The recruits joked that a borrowed blanket was larceny of equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们开玩笑说，借来一床毯子就算是偷窃装备。
senses.why: Barracks humour keeps the solemn legal word for small everyday grabs, giving the joke its edge.
senses.whyCN: 军营里的幽默把这个庄重的法律词用在日常小事上，玩笑的力道正来自这种落差。

intro.en: Larceny came into English through legal French from Latin latrocinium, meaning robbery, which grew from latro, a hired soldier or bandit.
intro.cn: larceny 经法律法语进入英语，来自拉丁语 latrocinium（抢夺、抢劫），而该词源于 latro（雇佣兵、强盗）。

items.en: Latro first meant a hired soldier or mercenary, and by the classical period it meant a bandit or robber.
items.cn: latro 最初指受雇的兵士或雇佣兵，到古典拉丁语时期已指强盗、劫匪。

items.en: Latrocinium named robbery or banditry and the plunder that went with it.
items.cn: latrocinium 指抢劫、匪盗行为以及随之而来的掠夺。

items.en: Legal French carried the word into a noun for theft of goods, losing the sense of armed raiding.
items.cn: 法律法语把它带进一个表示窃取财物的名词，原先做强盗的意思逐渐消失。

items.en: The law courts of medieval England used the Anglo-French form, and it entered written English records.
items.cn: 中古英格兰的法庭使用盎格鲁法语的词形，这一形式进入了英语的书面记录。

items.en: The word appears in English with the plain sense of theft, while robbery kept the sense of taking by force.
items.cn: 该词以「偷窃」的单纯含义出现在英语里，而表示抢夺的词仍保留使用武力的意思。

items.en: Common law judges defined it by the taking and carrying away of another person goods, and modern statutes set the value line between petty and grand.
items.cn: 普通法法官用「取走并带离他人财物」来界定它，现代成文法又用金额界线区分轻窃与重大盗窃。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root and the legal family; the second group holds the other offences that neighbours of this word in court.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个拉丁词根与法律词族；第二组是与这个词在法庭上常常并列的其他罪名。

entries.definition: relating to theft, or given to stealing
entries.definitionCN: 与盗窃有关的，或有偷窃倾向的。

entries.definition: a person who commits theft; used in informal and military speech
entries.definitionCN: 实施盗窃的人，多见于口语与军中说法。

entries.definition: an archaic word for robbery, closer to the Latin source
entries.definitionCN: 一个古老的词，指抢夺，更接近拉丁语词源。

entries.definition: the combined label used in crime reports for all theft offences
entries.definitionCN: 犯罪统计中把各类盗窃合并使用的标签。

entries.definition: the general word for taking things that belong to others
entries.definitionCN: 指取走他人财物的通用说法。

entries.definition: taking property by force or threat, which this word excludes
entries.definitionCN: 以武力或威胁夺取财物，而这个词强调不含暴力。

entries.definition: entering a building unlawfully with intent to commit a crime
entries.definitionCN: 非法进入建筑物并意图犯罪。

normalIntro.en: Larceny comes from Latin for a bandit, and the law narrowed it to quiet theft of goods.
normalIntro.cn: larceny 源于拉丁语中「强盗」一词，法律把它收窄为不声不响地窃取财物。

normal.en: The Latin root latro means bandit, so this word began as raiding and became stealing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 latro 意为强盗，所以这个词从夺掠变成了偷窃。

normal.en: Petty larceny and grand larceny are the two ends of a value line drawn by statute.
normal.cn: 轻窃与重大盗窃是成文法按金额划出的两端。

normal.en: Robbery needs force, larceny does not, which is why the two words sit side by side in court lists.
normal.cn: 抢劫需要武力，盗窃不需要，两词因此常并列出现在法庭清单上。

normal.en: The adjective larcenous describes a person with stealing habits, not the crime itself.
normal.cn: 形容词 larcenous 描述有偷窃习气的人，而不是罪名本身。

normal.en: Larceny keeps its Latin sense of carried away goods, as in the legal phrase taking and carrying away.
normal.cn: larceny 保留了「被带走之物」的拉丁意思，普通法里就写「取走并带离」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand slipping a purse from a bag while the crowd looks elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手趁人群看向别处，把钱包从包里抽走。

abstract.en: Think of a line on a chart: small theft on one side, large theft on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的一条线：一侧是小额盗窃，另一侧是大额盗窃。

abstract.en: A lie can open the door for the thief, but the law still calls it theft.
abstract.cn: 一个谎言能为窃贼打开门，法律仍把它叫作盗窃。

examples.en: Under state law, taking a bicycle without permission may count as larceny.
examples.cn: 按该州法律，未经允许骑走一辆自行车可能算作盗窃。

examples.en: Grand larceny charges were filed after the documents were sold.
examples.cn: 在文件被出售之后，有关部门以重大盗窃罪名提起诉讼。

examples.en: The history of the crime shows how petty larceny grew into a separate category.
examples.cn: 这项罪名的历史显示，轻窃如何演变出一个独立类别。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉森尼」——小偷「拉」开门「森」森地溜走，「尼」字收尾像偷偷藏起来：盗窃；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 latro（雇佣兵；强盗）→ latrocinium（抢夺；匪盗行为）→ 古法语法律用语（窃取财物）→ 盎格鲁法语 → 英语 larceny（盗窃罪），词根义由「强盗的夺掠」收窄为「偷窃」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the legal name of the crime, then split it by value, by the act of taking, by the absence of force, by deception, by stolen power and finally by military slang.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从罪名的法律名称开始，随后按金额、按取走的动作、按不含暴力、按欺骗手段、按被盗的电力燃气，最后按军中俚语依次展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sliding someone else purse into a pocket while nobody watches.
core.cn: 核心意象：趁无人注意，一只手把别人的钱包塞进自己的口袋。

branches.en: THE NAMED OFFENCE: the criminal case itself is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 被点名的罪名：犯罪案件本身是最核心的义项。

branches.en: TWO ENDS OF A SCALE: the value of what is taken decides which label applies.
branches.cn: 同一刻度的两端：被拿之物的价值决定适用哪个标签。

branches.en: THE ACT WITHOUT FORCE: taking and carrying away quietly is what the law requires.
branches.cn: 不施暴力的动作：安静地取走并带离正是法律要求的要件。

branches.en: DECEPTION AND STOLEN POWER: lies and metered supplies can also be the object of theft.
branches.cn: 欺骗与被盗能源：谎言和计量供应的东西也能成为盗窃对象。

branches.en: BARRACKS HUMOUR: a solemn legal word used for a small grab.
branches.cn: 军营里的幽默：庄重的法律词被用在顺手拿点小事上。

intro.en: The word is a Latin legal noun that reached English through French courts; its English family includes larcenous, larcenously and larcenist.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法国法庭传入英语的拉丁法律名词，英语词族包括 larcenous、larcenously 与 larcenist。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin forms are relevant: latro the bandit, latrocinium the robbery, and the Latin adjective latrocinialis, which is the ultimate model of the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 相关的拉丁词形有三个：表示强盗的 latro、表示抢劫的 latrocinium，以及后来的拉丁形容词，它正是英语形容词最终的模板。

items.example: Latro is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: latro 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 盗窃；尤指不含暴力的窃取
items.example: It keeps the legal sense of taking goods.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了取走财物的法律含义。

items.example: The ending makes the borrowed noun fit English patterns.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾使借来的名词符合英语的模式。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix builds the adjective larcenous.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成形容词 larcenous。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成副词。

items.example: The suffix forms the noun for a thief.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成指窃贼的名词。

items.example: It marks the lighter half of the crime scale.
items.exampleCN: 它标出罪案轻重刻度中较轻的一头。

items.example: It marks the heavier half of the scale.
items.exampleCN: 它标出刻度中较重的一头。

items.example: It is the everyday word that this legal term sharpens.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个法律术语所精确化的日常词。

latinEntries.meaning: to serve as a mercenary, to rob
